# FINDINGS — evidence-backed, with ladder results

Format: F<N> | territory | file:line | failure scenario | ladder result | status (FIXED/ESCALATED/OWNER-DECISION) | proof

## STATUS legend (normalized 2026-08-04, `scripts/findings-ledger-gate.sh` enforces this)

Every data row carries a normalized, machine-checkable trailer appended after
its original (historical, free-text) fields: ` | STATUS: <TOKEN> (was:
<original-text>) [| NEXT ACTION: <text>]`. The original fields are left
intact for provenance; the trailer is the ONE place a reader or a script
should look for "is this closed."

- **TERMINAL (closed, nothing owed):** `FIXED`, `DELETED`, `OWNER-DECISION`, `MOOT`
- **OPEN (something still owed):** `OPEN`, `CONFIRMED-STILL-LIVE`, `ESCALATED`, `PARTIAL`, `NEEDS-TRIAGE`

**Bucket rule (mechanical):** TERMINAL = {FIXED, DELETED, OWNER-DECISION,
MOOT}; every other STATUS token is OPEN and MUST carry a ` | NEXT ACTION:
<text>` segment on the same row. `NEEDS-TRIAGE` means: open, but the row's
own text did not state an actionable next step — do not infer one, retriage
the row itself first.

F101 | api-identity-money | apps/api/src/modules/billing/billing.service.ts:274-279 + apps/api/src/config/configuration.ts:208 + apps/api/src/modules/entitlements/entitlement.service.ts:402 | A PAYING CUSTOMER CAN BE 403'd. The RevenueCat entitlement id is translated by `reverseEntitlementMap.get(raw) ?? raw` — an unmapped vendor id silently BECOMES our entitlement code. The grant is then written under that code, while `accessVerdict()` only ever asks about `this.defaultCode`. So a purchase whose RC entitlement identifier is not in REVENUECAT_ENTITLEMENT_MAP mints a live, paid grant the paywall never looks at. Config makes this likely, not hypothetical: the map DEFAULTS to a guessed pair `'premium:premium_monthly'`, and plans/payments-ideal-shape.md:196 contemplates the owner using `premium:premium` instead. | LADDER: compensates for not knowing RC's identifier at code-write time. Bedrock: the ledger is denominated in OUR vocabulary; a vendor id we cannot translate is an UNKNOWN, and minting a grant from an unknown is the same error class as `hasAccess` returning true on failure — inventing an assertion from absent information, which access-verdict.ts already rederived away one level up. Rederive: translation returns `mapped(code) | unknown(vendorId)`; `unknown` records the billing event FAILED (`unmapped_entitlement:<id>`) and rethrows so RC redelivers after the map is fixed; the legal code set is one closed declaration and `syncSubscriptionGrant` refuses anything outside it; the seeded default map value is deleted (unconfigured is unconfigured, not a guess). Red team: makes an invisible paid grant unrepresentable; still relies on the owner setting the map, but now fails LOUD (failed rows + retrying webhook) instead of a customer paying for a 403. | FIXED (D1 — owner-ratified 2026-08-02: adopt the shape) — translation is a SUM TYPE (billing/revenuecat-entitlement-map.ts): `mapped(code) | unknown(vendorId)`, no fallback. An unmapped RC id records the billing event FAILED as `unmapped_entitlement:<id>` and RETHROWS (RC redelivers); the same law now covers the TRANSFER/subscriber-fetch path, which carried the identical `?? rcId` passthrough. The guessed default map `'premium:premium_monthly'` is DELETED from configuration.ts — unconfigured means nothing translates. Parsing is STRICT and runs in the constructor, so a malformed map REFUSES BOOT (also refuses one vendor id mapping to two codes). The legal codes are one closed, derived union (default code + declared codes), exposed as `entitlementCodes`. PROOF: revenuecat-entitlement-map.spec.ts, 8 pass, incl. 'RED — an unmapped id records the event FAILED and RETHROWS' (asserts syncSubscriptionGrant NOT called, under any code) and 'an UNSET map translates nothing'. SURPRISE: billing-webhooks.spec.ts's harness defaulted entitlementMap to `''` and every test still translated — the F101 defect visible in the fixture itself; the harness now carries a real map. RESIDUAL CLOSED (owner-ruled 2026-08-03, D1-residual: PREMIUM IS THE ONLY PRODUCT, EVER). `RevenueCatEntitlementMap.parse` now REFUSES AT BOOT any entry whose `ourCode` differs from the default code, naming the offending code, the code accessVerdict() actually consults, and the single-product law. Consequence: the old 'one vendor id maps to two of our codes' check became unreachable (every surviving code IS the default) and was deleted rather than left as an untestable guard — its spec case feeds the same input and now hits the new refusal. SPEC: refusal + message content + happy path + default-code-relativity (the refusal is relative to config, not to the literal 'premium'); RED-proved by neutering the condition — 3 cases fail. | proof: entitlement.service.ts:402 reads only defaultCode; billing.service.ts:278-279 `?? rawEntitlement`; configuration.ts:208 seeded default. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F102 | api-identity-money | apps/api/src/modules/identity/auth/optional-clerk-auth.guard.ts:9 + apps/api/src/modules/entitlements/paywall-coverage.audit.ts:76-79 | THE BOOT AUDIT'S MARKER LIES BY OMISSION. `@BearsRequestUser()` asserts an unconditional fact, but OptionalClerkAuthGuard sets `request.user` ONLY when a token is present. The audit treats any marker-bearing guard as coverage, so a route guarded solely by OptionalClerkAuthGuard and lacking `@AllowUnentitled` PASSES boot — and then 403s every anonymous caller the moment ENTITLEMENT_GATING=enforce. That is precisely the incident class the audit exists to prevent. No live gap today (all five current OptionalClerkAuthGuard routes also carry @AllowUnentitled) — correct by discipline, not by construction. | LADDER: compensates for there being no static way to know whether a guard produces a user. Bedrock: "reachable anonymously" is a property of the ROUTE, not the guard, and guards come in three kinds, not two: always-authenticates, maybe-authenticates, never. A two-valued marker cannot express the middle one, so it rounds it to the dangerous value. Rederive: replace the boolean marker with `@AuthenticationEffect('required'|'optional'|'none')`; a route is covered iff some guard is 'required' OR it is @AllowUnentitled; an 'optional'-only route fails boot with "OptionalClerkAuthGuard admits anonymous callers — add @AllowUnentitled()". Red team: today's correct-by-luck pairing becomes unbypassable; a forgotten annotation defaults to 'none' and fails boot loudly; the only new failure is over-declaring 'optional' on a required guard, which forces a visible, harmless @AllowUnentitled. | FIXED (D2) — @AuthenticationEffect('required'|'optional'|'none') replaces the boolean marker; boot refuses an optional-only route naming it + the fix. Runtime behavior unchanged (boot-time only). PROOF: paywall-coverage.audit.spec.ts, 11 pass, incl. 'RED — an optional-only route admits anonymous callers and is reported', 'an optional-only route FAILS BOOT, naming the route and the fix', 'an optional guard PLUS @AllowUnentitled is covered, and boots'. user-bearing-guard.ts DELETED. | proof: executed spec (scratch, removed) — `bearsRequestUser(OptionalClerkAuthGuard) === true` and `uncoveredRoutes() === []` for a controller guarded only by a conditional marker-bearing guard; both assertions PASSED. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F103 | api-identity-money | apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma access_grants CHECK `access_grants_day_xor_absolute` | THE CONSTRAINT IS NAND, NOT XOR, AND THE COMMENT SAYS XOR. Live definition (verified against the local mirror): `CHECK (granted_days IS NULL OR expires_at IS NULL)` — it permits a row with BOTH null. entitlement.service.ts:108-110 documents it as "schema-enforced XOR". Both-null is how LIFETIME is spelled, so a day-grant row that lost its `granted_days` is indistinguishable from a lifetime grant: `deriveSummary` classifies `grantedDays === null` as absolute, finds `expiresAt === null`, and returns unbounded access. The emptiest possible row is the most powerful state. | LADDER: compensates for encoding three shapes in two nullable columns. Bedrock: there are three grant shapes (absolute-with-expiry, lifetime, day-count); a representation must make each one say its own name, and the accidental/empty state must be the LEAST powerful, never the most. Rederive: an explicit `kind` column ('absolute'|'lifetime'|'day') with a CHECK pinning each shape's columns exactly, so a row that sets nothing is illegal rather than immortal. A source-list-based CHECK is rejected: it would duplicate GRANT_POLICY in SQL. Red team: makes accidental-lifetime unrepresentable; costs a migration on money data; the existing code paths cannot currently produce both-null (grant() rejects days<=0 and demands expiresAt|lifetime), so this is a representation defect, not a live bug — which is exactly when it is cheap to fix. | FIXED (D3 — owner-ratified 2026-08-02) — migration 20260803020000_access_grant_kind adds `access_grants.kind` ('lifetime'|'days'|'window') with a per-kind CHECK (`access_grants_kind_shape`) pinning each shape's columns exactly; the NAND `access_grants_day_xor_absolute` is dropped. The backfill DERIVES kind from column shape (days-set→days, window-set→window, both-null→lifetime) and the migration then ASSERTS totality in a DO block — row count == classified count == count in the union, else RAISE and roll back. Code reads `kind` explicitly: deriveSummary partitions on `grant.kind`, the lifetime short-circuit tests `kind === 'lifetime'` rather than an absent expiry, and every write (grant, syncSubscriptionGrant create AND update) states its kind. APPLIED to the local mirror: comp→lifetime 2, subscription→window 2, trial_base→window 1, zero unclassified. Fresh-DB replay of all 218 migrations clean. PROOF: the DB-backed entitlement.service.spec.ts, 12 pass, incl. 'RED — a day-grant that loses its granted_days can no longer become immortal' (the DB rejects the both-null row with access_grants_kind_shape) and 'every write NAMES its shape'. | proof: `pg_get_constraintdef` on the local mirror. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F105 | api-identity-money | apps/api/src/modules/moderation/moderation.service.ts:35-43 | FAIL-OPEN MODERATION, WITH THE FIX ALREADY WRITTEN ELSEWHERE IN THE REPO. On any LLM error the decision is `{allowed:true, reason:'moderation_error'}` — a boolean return type that cannot say "I could not find out", so its catch block invents an assertion, globally, for every caller (username claims, poll/photo content). The comment concedes it and defers. | LADDER: this is verbatim the defect access-verdict.ts already rederived: three honest answers, not two. Bedrock: allowed / blocked / indeterminate; the policy for indeterminate belongs to the CALL SITE, because a username claim (retryable, cheap to refuse) and a comment post (availability wins) genuinely differ. Rederive: `ModerationVerdict = allowed | blocked(reason) | indeterminate(cause,message)` plus `resolveModeration(verdict, 'allow'|'hold')`, mirroring resolveVerdict exactly — the pattern is proven and tested in this codebase, it simply never reached moderation. Red team: makes a global lie unrepresentable; each surface must state its policy out loud; nothing changes behaviourally until a call site chooses 'hold'. | FIXED (D9 — owner-ratified 2026-08-02) — moderation-verdict.ts adopts the access-verdict shape verbatim: `allowed | blocked(reason) | indeterminate(cause,message)` plus `resolveModeration(verdict, 'allow'|'hold')`, documented in the same style and for the same reason. The catch block no longer invents `{allowed:true, reason:'moderation_error'}`; it logs the outage LOUD and returns indeterminate. ALL SEVEN call sites are WRITE paths and each states its policy out loud as `'hold'` with a per-site comment (polls: description, user-supplied entity name, poll title, discussion question, comment create, comment edit; identity: checkAvailability, which claimUsername uses as its only gate). A refusal now names its cause, so 'the text was rejected' and 'the moderator was unreachable' are distinguishable: username gained the reason `moderation_unavailable`, distinct from `profanity`. No read surface calls moderation today; 'allow' exists and is spec'd for when one does. PROOF: moderation-verdict.spec.ts, 7 pass, incl. 'RED — a moderator outage is indeterminate, NOT an allow'. | proof: read; access-verdict.spec.ts is the working precedent. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F200 | api-ops | ops-dashboard.controller.ts:41-53 (@Get page route) + ops-token.guard.ts:31 + ops-dashboard.html.ts:3,141-163 | THE OWNER'S INCIDENT CONSOLE CANNOT BE OPENED BY THE OWNER. The HTML page is served by `@Get()` under the class-level `@UseGuards(OpsTokenGuard)`, and that guard reads the `x-ops-token` HEADER only. A browser cannot attach a custom header to a top-level navigation, so `GET /ops` from a browser is a 401 in every case — with no token, with the documented `?token=` bootstrap, and with any URL a bookmark could hold. The page's own delivery machinery is therefore unreachable code: the module doc at html.ts:3 advertises "stores the ?token= in localStorage on first visit", and the `tokenGate` prompt at :152-162 is the fallback for a visit that can never happen. Only a header-capable client (curl/fetch) can fetch the page, and such a client has no use for HTML. This is the shipped consequence of a CORRECT fix applied at one level only: red team #7 removed the `?token=` branch because a query-string secret is recorded by the logging interceptor, the exception filter, Sentry, browser history and proxy logs — true, and it must not come back — but the PAGE's delivery was never rederived to match, so the surface was hardened into inaccessibility. | LADDER: the guard compensates for there being one credential mechanism for two genuinely different resources. Bedrock: the JSON routes carry DATA and are called by a header-capable client, so a header is the right credential; the PAGE carries no data at all and is fetched by a NAVIGATION, whose only credential mechanism the browser can supply automatically is a cookie. One guard cannot serve both without either leaking the secret (query) or refusing the browser (header) — which is exactly the fork this code is stuck on. Rederive: a one-time bootstrap route (`GET /ops/enter?token=…`) that validates, sets an HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict session cookie, and 302s to `/ops` WITHOUT the query string, so the secret never reaches a logged URL and never reaches JS; the page route accepts the cookie, the JSON routes accept cookie OR header; the page's localStorage token handling and tokenGate are then deleted outright (the browser holds the credential, not the document). Red team: makes "the console is unreachable in an incident" impossible and makes "the secret is in a logged URL" impossible at the same time — today's design only achieves the second. The bootstrap URL is still logged once, so it must be single-use-per-visit and the cookie short-lived; that is strictly better than every subsequent fetch carrying it. New failure: a cookie is ambient authority, so the JSON routes need the existing CSRF posture checked for the one POST (alerts ack). | FIXED (D19) | PROOF: executed Nest+Fastify probe, now PERMANENT as ops-browser-access.spec.ts (8/8 green). `GET /ops/enter?token=<correct>` => 302, Location == `/ops` carrying NEITHER the token NOR `token=`, Set-Cookie `ops_session=<expiry>.<hmac>` with HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict and NOT containing the secret; that cookie then opens BOTH `GET /ops` (200, real HTML) and `GET /ops/api/summary` (200). The three original defect assertions still hold as regression cases: naked `GET /ops` => 401, `GET /ops?token=<correct>` => 401 (the query-string secret stays dead), header => 200 UNCHANGED, and a PRESENT-but-wrong header still 401s (the cookie never widens a failed header check). OpsTokenGuard's file is byte-unchanged; OpsAccessGuard delegates to it whenever a header is present. Absent env => 404 on page, JSON and bootstrap alike. Forged, EXPIRED, and rotated-secret cookies all 401. Page's localStorage bootstrap + tokenGate DELETED — the document now holds no credential at all. NOTE FOR OWNER: `Secure` is unconditional per the binding constraint, so cookie access requires https (staging/prod); plain-http localhost must use the header path. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F201 | api-ops | ops-dashboard.controller.ts / ops-token.guard.spec.ts:45-67 | THE GUARD PROTECTING THE OPS CONSOLE HAD NO TEST THAT COULD SHOW RED ON THE COMPARISON. Three of the five cases ("401s a missing token", "401s a wrong token", "REFUSES a matching ?token= query param") supply the token via `query`, which a header-only guard ignores — so all three exercise the SAME branch, "no x-ops-token header". There was no case where a header was PRESENT but WRONG. MUTATION-PROVEN: with `constantTimeEquals` replaced by `return true`, so that any header value whatsoever opens the dashboard, the suite passed 5/5. F202 | api-signals | signal-demand-read.service.ts (14 occurrences of `LEFT JOIN entity_redirects` + `COALESCE(r.to_entity_id, …)`) vs :608-628 lastEntityViewAt; corroborated by signal-demand-read.territory.spec.ts:145 | THE LEDGER'S IDENTITY LAW IS A CONVENTION EVERY READER MUST REMEMBER, AND ONE READER ALREADY FORGOT. New failure: a view adds a planner hop on hot autocomplete reads — must be measured against the current sargable-expansion path before adopting, and if it loses, the fallback is the weaker-but-real fix (make `dailyActsCteSql` own the redirect join instead of accepting it as a parameter, and route every non-CTE reader through a single `resolvedSubjectSql()` builder). | FIXED (D20a — the fragment-home fallback, NOT the view) | PROOF: new signals/subject-identity.ts owns `redirectJoinSql` / `resolvedSubjectSql` / `subjectMatchesSql`; all 14 hand-copied sites in signal-demand-read.service.ts converted, and the LIVE OMISSION at lastEntityViewAt fixed (it now joins and compares through `subjectMatchesSql`, so a merged loser id's history is visible again). subject-identity-lockdown.spec.ts is MUTATION-PROVEN: planting a hand-rolled `COALESCE(r.to_entity_id, s.subject_id)` + `LEFT JOIN entity_redirects` in a scratch file turned it RED naming `modules/signals/scratch-mutation-probe.ts`; probe removed, 7/7 green. F203 | api-signals | signals.service.ts:160-180 (record) + 7 injecting services | "RECORD THE SIGNAL" IS A CONVENTION, NOT A CHOKEPOINT — AND THE LEDGER IS THE ONE RECORD (§3). `record()` returns `void` and is called as a bare fire-and-forget statement by 7 services (search, on-demand-request, search-query-interpretation, polls, history, user-lists, signals.controller). Rederive (two candidate shapes, both weaker than I would like — flagging the problem more confidently than the solution): (a) type-level — the operations that constitute acts return an `Act<K>` token that only `record()` consumes, so an unrecorded act is an unused value a lint rule can fail on; (b) boot-audit — the same shape as the paywall-coverage audit that already exists in this repo (entitlements/paywall-coverage.audit.ts): enumerate the routes that mutate user-visible state, require each to declare either a `@RecordsSignal('kind')` or an explicit `@NoSignal('reason')`, and refuse to boot on an undeclared one. A USER-ACT ROUTE is structural: mutating verb + a guard declaring @AuthenticationEffect('required') + not @AllowUnentitled. BOTH DIRECTIONS proven by signal-coverage.audit.spec.ts (5/5): an undeclared act route throws at boot naming the route AND the fix; either declaration passes; an EMPTY @NoSignal reason is NOT a declaration; a GET, a public route and an operator route are not asked; and controllers-with-zero-act-routes throws the not-vacuously-green error. EXECUTED census over the REAL controllers (reflect-metadata probe, removed): 53 user-act routes, 0 UNDECLARED, and all 9 declared kinds mapped faithfully to the 7 recording services — search/autocomplete_selection/on_demand_ask at SearchController.run+runNatural, search at recordCacheAttribution, entity_view at both HistoryController writes, favorite_added at UserListsController.addFavoriteItem+addListItem, poll_created/poll_comment/poll_vote at PollsController, viewport_dwell at SignalsController. Zero behavior change: declarations are metadata only. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F204 | api-signals | integrity/sybil-cluster-report.service.ts:606 | THE ONE PLACE IN THE REPO THAT COMPARES `signals.occurred_at` WITHOUT THE COERCION THE MODULE WROTE FOR IT. `AND s.occurred_at >= now() - make_interval(days => 30)` compares a NAIVE-UTC column against a timestamptz, so Postgres coerces the right side to the SESSION time zone's wall clock. signals/sql-instant.ts exists for precisely this column and this reason, and every other consumer uses it. Measured on the local mirror (session TZ America/Chicago, `occurred_at` confirmed `timestamp without time zone`): the boundary is `2026-07-03 20:39` under Chicago vs `2026-07-04 01:39` under UTC — the sybil sweep's 30-day lookback silently slides by the server's UTC offset. F205 | api-signals + api-ops | signal-demand-aggregate.service.ts:201-207, signal-partition-maintenance.service.ts:78-86, integrity/sybil-cluster-report.service.ts:116-122 | THREE CRONS WHOSE DEATH IS INVISIBLE, ONE OF WHICH SILENTLY STOPS THE LEDGER. All three catch everything and emit a log line only; none emits an ops_alert, though OpsAlertsService is the codebase's single owner-attention seam, is already injected into the sybil service, and is described in its own doc as existing for exactly these chokepoints. The consequences are not equal and the partition one is severe: partition maintenance keeps `signals` RANGE partitions ahead of the clock, and its own header states that an insert into a month with no partition FAILS the write while the §3 law makes the writer swallow that failure — so a dead cron eventually means every signal is silently dropped, observable only as a `warn` per write and a ledger that quietly stops growing. The repo has already ratified the principle ("every metric must be able to show RED") and already built the mechanism. Rederive: each catch keeps swallowing AND calls `opsAlerts.emit({severity, kind, dedupeKey})` — `critical` for partition maintenance (it can lose user acts), `warn` for the other two, each with a dedupeKey so a persistent failure nags once rather than every tick, which the emit path already supports. PLUS the un-foolable shape: `assertLeadPartitionExists()` runs daily and alerts CRITICAL when the now+1-month partition is absent, which fires on a scheduler that simply stopped as readily as on a DDL that threw. LIVE PROOF on the local mirror inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK: the assertion's exact query returned 1 with `signals_p2026_09` present, 0 after DETACH+DROP of that future partition, and 1 again after ROLLBACK (mirror untouched). Unit-proven both ways in signal-partition-maintenance.service.spec.ts (silent when present, CRITICAL when absent, WARN when the check itself throws). | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F350 | api-places-enrichment | places-promotion.service.ts:383-398,539-551 + tomtom-chain-probe.adapter.ts:354-360,602-607 vs governance.service.ts:721-726 | "A CONSUMED DRAW" IS DEFINED THREE DIFFERENT WAYS IN ONE FLOW, AND THE TWO THAT COST MONEY DISAGREE WITH THE ONE THAT SPENDS IT. governance.drawWithOutcome debits the pool on a THROW ("we conservatively debit 1 — the request likely reached the vendor"). The adapter's `recordDraw()` (api_usage_ledger) runs ONLY after a non-null response, so a transport error writes no ledger row. The promotion service's `draws.scarce` (the CAMPAIGN ENVELOPE) is likewise never incremented on the transport-error path — while promoteOne's own docstring states it meters "promoted, consumed-draw miss, wrong-entity reject, no-rings, TRANSPORT ERROR", and the catch block's comment asserts "the draw was conservatively debited". Both claims are false of the code beside them. Consequence: on a TomTom fault the rate pool is debited, the campaign envelope is not, and cost-reconcile cannot see the draw at all — the same "summed the wrong column" class as the $118 Places lesson, one level down, and the same class as the campaign envelope that "was sized for Places spend it never debited" (round-six cost #4). | LADDER: compensates for the draw being counted at three levels that were each built at a different time, with no shared definition. Bedrock: a vendor draw is ONE event; who was charged is a property of the draw, not of the caller that noticed it. Rederive: `governance.drawWithOutcome` is the only place that knows whether the vendor was reached, so it should RETURN that fact — `{admitted, value, drawsConsumed}` — and both the ledger write and the campaign meter should hang off that single return rather than off each caller's guess. The adapter's recordDraw and the promotion service's `draws` counter then stop being independent re-derivations of a fact the governor already computed. Red team: makes under-metering unrepresentable rather than merely untested; costs a signature change at ~8 governed call sites; the new failure is OVER-metering when a request genuinely never left the process (connect-refused), which is the conservative direction the pool already chose deliberately. | FIXED (D51, owner-ruled 2026-08-03 — the metering GAP is CLOSED, in the recommendation's own shape). `governance.drawWithOutcome` now takes `onDrawConsumed` and fires it EXACTLY ONCE per ADMITTED draw — success path AND throw path, never on a denial — and the api_usage_ledger write plus the campaign envelope both hang off that single announcement instead of re-deriving 'a draw happened' from a response only the happy path has. Deleted: three post-hoc `recordDraw(op)` calls in the adapter and both manual `draws.scarce += 1` increments in the promotion service. Accepted cost, exactly as the finding's red team framed it: a connect-refused is now metered, which is OVER-metering in the conservative direction the pool already chose. A meter that throws cannot fail the draw it meters. PROOF: 4 new governance cases (announce on success, announce on throw, NOT on denial, meter-throw is swallowed) + a promotion case proving a transport-errored draw is charged to the campaign; MUTATION-PROVEN — deleting the throw-path announcement turns exactly one test RED. || PRIOR PASS: FIXED-PARTIAL (D29a accounting-truth half landed 2026-08-03) | PROOF(pass1): read all three; governance.service.ts:721-726 debits in `catch`, adapter recordDraw is after the null-check, promotion `draws.scarce += 1` appears only at :558 and :573, never in the :539 catch. || PASS-3 PROOF (D29a): the two draw words are DEFINED ONCE, in governance.drawWithOutcome's docstring — ADMITTED (pool, debits on throw) vs ANSWERED (ledger + campaign, hang off a non-null response) — and all three meters now state which they count. promoteOne's docstring no longer lists 'transport error' among metered exits; the :539 catch no longer claims a debit the ledger/campaign never made; the adapter's recordDraw says ANSWERED. Spend behaviour byte-unchanged (no call site added, removed or reordered); yarn build + full suite green. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F351 | api-places-enrichment | apps/api/src/modules/places/places-containment.integration.spec.ts:407,433 | THE ONLY DB-BACKED TEST IN THE REPO DID NOT COMPILE, AND BOTH MECHANISMS THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT WERE DARK. This is the file whose own header says a law enforced by the database has to be proven against the database, and that it "FAILS LOUDLY without [DATABASE_URL] rather than skipping: a silently-skipped test proves nothing, which is the exact disease this file treats". It was not skipping — it was failing to compile (`new SignalDemandAggregateService(prisma, logger)` against a constructor that gained an `opsAlerts` parameter, almost certainly from the concurrent api-signals pass landing F205). It is excluded from `yarn test` by testPathIgnorePatterns, so only `yarn test:db` runs it, and only CI runs `yarn test:db` — and CI dies at the `Lint` step, which precedes both `Type check` and `test:db`, on every one of the last 6 runs. So the twelve containment laws — including the largest-gap antimeridian law that this very file proved RED twice before its fix — have been unguarded. EXECUTED: `npx tsc --noEmit` reports these two lines as the ONLY type errors in the entire API. | LADDER: compensates for nothing; it is rot admitted by a gate nobody watches. Bedrock: a guard that cannot run is not a guard, and "excluded from the default test run" plus "the only lane that runs it is behind an earlier failing step" is two independent single points of failure on the repo's most expensive-to-rebuild knowledge. Rederive: (a) run the integration lane BEFORE lint in CI, or at minimum make lint non-blocking for the test steps, so a green-tests signal cannot be hidden behind a formatting failure; (b) since `yarn type-check` DOES catch this class in one second, make type-check the first CI step; (c) better still, delete the testPathIgnorePatterns exclusion and have the spec skip-with-failure on a missing DATABASE_URL exactly as its header already promises, so `yarn test` locally surfaces the breakage the moment it happens. Red team: (a)+(b) are pure ordering with no downside; (c) makes every local `yarn test` need a database, which is a real cost — so (b) is the one I would land first, and it is free. | FIXED (test-only; production untouched) — added the missing OpsAlertsService stub argument at both call sites. Before the fix: "Test suite failed to run", 0 tests. The CI-ordering half remains OWNER-DECISION. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

(b) compensates for two SKUs and one method; bedrock: the field mask determines the price, so "which mask" is not a call-site option, it is the identity of the operation — `getPlaceDetailsRefresh()` and `getPlaceDetailsFull()` as separate methods make a refresh that bills enterprise impossible to write. RED-proved: relabelling the spec fixture back to 'grounding.refresh' fails 2 spend-analytics cases. The CALL is byte-identical — mask unchanged, no campaign capture. || PASS-3 PROOF (F352a, owner-ruled 2026-08-03): (a) IS NOW FIXED. `currentCampaignId()` is captured into the expansion job payload and `runInWorkContext` re-established in the worker — the same mechanism the primary-enrichment and attribute-ontology lanes use, and the bulk paths that enqueue this work (city-reextract.runner:91, gemini-batch.service:676) already establish that context, so the capture is live rather than theoretical. F353 | api-places-enrichment | restaurant-location-enrichment.service.ts:2312-2448 (enrichSecondaryLocations) | THE `locationBias` PARAMETER OF SECONDARY EXPANSION IS DEAD, AND A RULED DESIGN IS BUILT ON THE BELIEF THAT IT IS LIVE. `enrichSecondaryLocations(entity, placeDetails, locationBias?)` has exactly ONE caller (:744) and it passes TWO arguments. `GooglePlacesService.findPlaceFromText` applies a bias only under `if (options.locationBias)`, so the live expansion is an UNBIASED GLOBAL text search for the brand name. plans/data-audit-2026-08.md's P2.2 research states the opposite as the cause of its class (b): "The brand is right; secondary expansion is LOCATION-BIASED so it never attached the other metro's branches" — and P2.2 rule 2 proposes spending a new per-mention Places call with the mention metro's bias to repair it. MEASURED on the local mirror, the premise does not hold: Chipotle 61 locations, Raising Cane's 58, Jet's Pizza 56, sweetgreen 39, Dunkin' 39 — all multi-metro, all one domain, all expanded. What the data DOES show is (i) 23 restaurants sit at or past the per-run cap of 60 with a maximum of 121, i.e. large brands hold an ARBITRARY, RANKING-DEPENDENT, TRUNCATED sample of their real branches (Chipotle has thousands), and (ii) a separate real class the research did not name: `Shake Shack 1700 Broadway - 53rd & 7th` has ONE location, because when Google's displayName for the grounding place is branch-qualified, the brand-purity gate `restaurantNamesAgree(canonicalName, siblingName)` rejects every genuine sibling. | LADDER: the dead parameter compensates for nothing — it is residue that makes the code READ as biased, which is how the research reached a wrong diagnosis; that is the real cost of dead code here. Rederive: before P2.2 ships, expansion must either be complete or must SAY it is incomplete — a per-brand `expansionComplete` fact (set false when a run hits the cap or the name gate rejected candidates), and the metro test must abstain (adopt, never mint) whenever it is false. The name gate should compare against the entity's BRAND name (normalizeBrandName already exists in this file) rather than Google's branch-qualified displayName. Red team: this does not weaken brand purity — an abstain is strictly safer than a mint — and it removes the need for rule 2's extra per-mention Places call in the common case, which is the cheaper answer to the same problem. | FIXED (D28 APPROVE, 2026-08-03) — the premise correction is recorded in plans/data-audit-2026-08.md:582-583 (locationBias dead; expansion global but CAP-TRUNCATED at 60); landed in c29265179 | PROOF: grep — one call site, two arguments; google-places.service.ts:637 `if (options.locationBias)`; psql on localhost/crave_search for the location counts, the 23-at-cap figure, and the Shake Shack row. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F354 | api-places-enrichment | restaurant-location-enrichment.service.ts:2442-2447 vs restaurant-secondary-location-expansion-queue.service.ts:49 | A RETRY POLICY THAT CAN NEVER FIRE, GUARDING A JOB THAT FAILS PARTWAY BY DESIGN. `enrichSecondaryLocations` wraps its entire paginated body — every Places call, every upsert — in one `catch` that logs a warning and returns void. The queue that drives it declares `attempts: 3`. Because the service can never throw, the job always completes successfully, so the three attempts are unreachable: a fault after page 1 leaves a brand permanently holding a partial branch set, the job is marked done, and nothing anywhere records that the set is partial. The failure and the success are the same observable. | LADDER: the catch compensates for the correct instinct that one brand's expansion must not kill the pass. Bedrock: not crashing and not telling anyone are different decisions, and only the first was made (the identical shape F205 names for the signals crons). Worse here, because the caller is a QUEUE that already implements the right behaviour — retry — and is prevented from using it. Rederive: let the loop throw; the queue's `attempts: 3` then means what it says, and per-page progress is already idempotent (upsert keyed on googlePlaceId, `seenPlaceIds` rebuilt from stored locations each run) so a retry resumes rather than repeats. If a swallow must remain, it must be visible in a RETURN value (`{complete: boolean}`) that the caller records — which is the same fact F353 needs for the metro test. Red team: throwing makes a vendor outage retry three times at Places cost instead of zero — that is the trade, and it is the one the queue's author already chose for the primary lane; the alternative (silent permanent truncation) is worse because it corrupts the location set that P2.2 will reason over. | FIXED (owner-ruled 2026-08-03, D32 escalation: YES to throwing) | PROOF: read; the catch at :2442 had no rethrow; queue `attempts: 3` at :49. || PASS-3 PROOF: the catch is GONE — `enrichSecondaryLocations` throws, the worker does not swallow, and the queue's attempts:3 is reachable for the first time. THE IDEMPOTENCE CLAIM WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED, and it was HALF FALSE: upserts keyed on the unique `googlePlaceId` and a `seenPlaceIds` rebuilt each attempt from a freshly re-read `include: { locations: true }` are real (single caller, restaurant-location-enrichment.service.ts:520-579), BUT the loop's `processedThisPage === 0` break meant a retry — whose page 1 is entirely already-stored — STOPPED AT PAGE 1 and never reached the page that faulted. The resume was a resume in name only. The break test now counts qualifying branches PRESENT on the page (`processedThisPage + alreadyStoredThisPage`), not rows WRITTEN, excluding the canonical place so a zero-branch brand still stops after page 1 and buys no second page. Two consequential side-effects, both named in code: `removeOnFail` 50->true (a retained failed job squats on the jobId and silently no-ops the next enqueue — harmless while nothing could fail, harmful the moment failure is real) and the primary lane's exponential backoff mirrored (three attempts back-to-back would triple a vendor blip's Places bill in seconds). Spend authority unchanged: same per-op ceilings, same 60-result cap. SPEC restaurant-secondary-location-expansion.spec.ts, 9 cases, 4 RED-proved by mutation: reinstating the worker's swallow, reverting the pagination-resume test, dropping the queue's campaign capture, and dropping the worker's runInWorkContext each fail exactly one case. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F355 | api-places-enrichment | restaurant-entity-merge.service.ts:183-219 (mergeLocations) + prisma/schema.prisma:136,154 | TWO SOURCES OF TRUTH FOR "THE PRIMARY LOCATION", AND THE UNCONSTRAINED ONE IS WRONG 398 TIMES. `core_entities.primary_location_id` is a real FK — structurally single. `core_restaurant_locations.is_primary` is a plain Boolean with only a non-unique index. Red team: deriving is strictly better (one truth, no drift, no migration risk beyond the drop); the index option is cheaper but keeps two facts in sync by constraint rather than by construction, and the merge bug would then throw instead of corrupting — loud, but it would need fixing anyway. | FIXED-PARTIAL (the PRODUCER is fixed 2026-08-03; the column drop + 398-row repair remain OWNER-DECISION) | PROOF(pass1): psql on localhost/crave_search — 398 restaurants with >1 is_primary; 0 FK/boolean disagreements across 6,848 restaurants with locations. || PASS-3 PROOF (D32): mergeLocations no longer decides primacy in the loop — moved rows land isPrimary:false, one primary is elected once, and every other row of the canonical is DEMOTED (updateMany), so the merge can no longer ADD primaries. The 398 existing rows and the column drop need a migration plus edits across the SEARCH module (~40 sites), which is outside this pass's four modules — STOPPED and reported rather than half-migrated. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F357 | api-places-enrichment | attribute-ontology.service.ts:160-290 + attribute-ontology.worker.ts:43 | THE ADJUDICATION LOOP HAS NO CEILING ON ITS OWN SIZE, AND ITS COST IS LINEAR IN A NUMBER NOBODY CHOSE. `buildPlan` issues one `placeAttribute` LLM call PER CANDIDATE (pass 1, concurrency 12), one more per NEW canonical (pass 2), and one `chooseAttributeName` per new canonical that absorbed synonyms (pass 3) — plus one embedding pass over every candidate AND every active canonical. Bedrock: correctness-independence justifies being LATE, not being UNBOUNDED; a job whose cost scales with a queue nobody bounds needs to state its own per-run size, and the ledger already prices these calls. Rederive: a per-run candidate cap (drain oldest-pending-first, leave the rest for the next tick — the debounce already re-fires), so the run size is a declared number rather than an emergent one; and, since the reload/re-extract campaigns already carry spend envelopes, adjudication triggered during a campaign should ride that campaign like the enrichment lane does. The alternative is that the first big re-extraction discovers the run size empirically, on the bill. | FIXED (bounded by an EXISTING pool 2026-08-03; the per-run SIZE cap refused as a new constant) | PROOF(pass1): read; no cap between :169 fetchAttributeRows (unfiltered by count) and the batch loop at :217; llm.service.ts:1369/:1954 confirm both calls carry caller profiles. || PASS-3 PROOF (D32): the adjudication job payload carries the enqueuing work's campaignId and the worker re-establishes it via runInWorkContext, so a run triggered during a reload/re-extract campaign debits that campaign's envelope (usage-ledger's meterCampaignSpend already attributes ambiently) and breaches like any other lane. NO new constant. The per-run candidate cap D32 also floated is NOT implemented and cannot be: every per-run ceiling is a number nobody has measured, and no existing governed pool expresses a run SIZE — recorded in buildPlan's docstring rather than invented. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F358 | api-places-enrichment | estimators/estimator-registry.ts:204-228, 63-65, 23-30, 94 | THE EXPLORATION MECHANISM THE REGISTRY _FORCES_ YOU TO DECLARE IS INVERTED AT THE ONE CASE IT EXISTS FOR — PLUS TWO DECLARED LAWS WITH NO IMPLEMENTATION AND ONE DEAD FIELD. `register()` refuses any self-gating estimator that does not declare an exploration mechanism (a genuinely good structural law). But `read()` computes `uncertainty = sqrt(variance / total)` from OBSERVED variance alone, so a subject with ZERO observations gets variance 0 and therefore uncertainty 0 — maximum confidence from no data. `EstimatorReading.uncertainty`'s own docstring says "Infinity when no data and no prior", and the staged-off branch twenty lines above correctly returns Infinity; the enabled branch returns 0. For `optimisticSelection` — documented as "a starved candidate can always re-demonstrate" — the upper-confidence bound of a never-observed subject is exactly the prior, which is BELOW that of any subject with real variance, so the starved candidate is ranked LAST. The mechanism does the opposite of its stated job. Separately: `versionBindings` is declared by 4 configs and read by NOTHING, and no API exists to change a bound version — so the header's law "a bound version change widens uncertainty / flags re-probe instead of silently mixing regimes" is asserted in prose and implemented nowhere; `hierarchy` is declared with four meanings ("Place-keyed estimators shrink along the places containment DAG") and never read by the registry — the shrinkage lives in PollSupplyEstimators.hierarchicalRead, which takes name+placeId explicitly and ignores `config.hierarchy`, so a second consumer calling plain `read()` on a 'placesDag' estimator silently gets no shrinkage and nothing says so; and `weightSquares` is incremented and decayed on every observation and never read at all. | LADDER: all four compensate for a primitive that was specified more completely than it was built (one commit, "Phase A"), and the type then made the unbuilt parts look built. Bedrock: a config field is a PROMISE the reader will honour; a field the reader ignores is worse than a missing feature because it silently converts a caller's correct declaration into a no-op. Rederive: (1) uncertainty must account for the prior's own dispersion so that n=0 yields the WIDEST interval, not the narrowest — the minimal honest form is to floor it by a prior-derived term that decays as nEffective grows, which is the same self-erasure the estimate already implements; (2) either implement version binding (a `bindVersion(name, value)` that widens or resets on change) or DELETE `versionBindings` and the header clause — a law with no enforcement is the always-green disease at the level of documentation; (3) move `hierarchicalRead` INTO the registry keyed off `config.hierarchy`, so declaring 'placesDag' does the thing (the poll module's implementation is the working reference); (4) delete `weightSquares`. Red team: (1) changes the numbers every consumer reads, so it needs the poll-supply specs re-baselined and is the only part with real blast radius; (2)-(4) are pure deletions or a lift-and-shift with none. | FIXED (D31, 2026-08-03) for limb (1); limbs (2)-(4) are OUT OF D31's SCOPE and still open | PROOF(pass1): EXECUTED (scratch spec, removed) — a never-observed subject on an `optimisticSelection` config returns `uncertainty = 0, priorWeight = 1`, and its UCB is 0.2 against a measured subject's 0.22, i.e. the starved candidate loses. Both assertions PASSED. grep confirms zero readers for `versionBindings`, `weightSquares`, and `config.hierarchy`. || PASS-3 PROOF (D31): uncertainty is Infinity whenever dispersion is UNMEASURED — a staged-off reader, or fewer than two effective observations (a spread needs two points; the threshold is definitional, not tuned). A zero-observation subject now carries the widest interval and WINS an optimistic-selection comparison. RED-proved: 3 of the 4 new estimator-registry cases fail against the pre-D31 registry (git stash + rerun). Consumers already guarded for non-finite uncertainty (poll-supply-controller.ts:139, poll-weekly-ritual.service.ts:920); poll-supply + weekly-ritual suites green unchanged. STILL OPEN: versionBindings, config.hierarchy and weightSquares remain declared-and-unread — D31 ruled only on the exploration inversion. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

The 1:1:1 invariant HOLDS on the local mirror: 22,770 places, 22,770 grounds, 22,770 promotion rows, ZERO places without a ground, and exactly 3 sketch-grade rows which are exactly the 3 unpromoted queue rows. The doc calls this "never falling back to a weaker judgment", which is true of the geometry but not of the availability; it is the F206 class. I am not escalating it because the consumer (a map header) genuinely prefers a degraded label to an error, but the honest shape is the same `{ok:false}` F206 proposes, decided at the call site. | - | psql 1:1:1 query on localhost/crave_search; places-containment.integration.spec.ts 12/12 green after F351's repair. | STATUS: MOOT (was: IDEAL-VERIFIED)

(c) The reconciler's 30-day TTL has no expiry test: the spec proves a cached region answers WITHIN the TTL, and the prune test only counts `deleteMany` calls — nothing proves an EXPIRED region re-probes, which is the arm that costs money when it is wrong in either direction (never re-probing suppresses discovery for 30 days; always re-probing is the spend-forever class the memory exists to prevent). Rederive: (a) assert the two query strings DIFFER; (b) assert the built SQL contains `@>` and not `= ANY`, and add a cyclic-DAG fixture that terminates; (c) advance the clock past NEGATIVE_OBSERVATION_TTL_MS and assert a probe fires. (a) The adapter spec's stale comments were the wrong half: the county qualifier is genuinely DEAD (forwardGeocodeMatch queries `name, subdivisionCode`), and the county is a RUNG OF ITS OWN — the fixture now carries a county name appearing nowhere else ('Gotham County') and the test asserts it appears in exactly ONE forward URL, its own rung's, never as a qualifier on another. (b) place-dag-read.spec now asserts `UNION` and NOT `UNION ALL`, and that the recursive JOIN line contains `@>` and not `= ANY` (the 13-17s -> 28ms GIN attribution), plus a cyclic-parent fixture that must TERMINATE. OPTIONS: (1) KEEP as owner-set constants — ratify 3/3 as a deliberate choice (matches the existing precedent for TEASER_SCORE_CEILING=9.9, also owner-set), record it once in the code as an owner constant rather than a bare literal. F400 | api-core | apps/api/src/shared/logging/logger.service.ts (whole file) vs logger.interface.ts + winston-logger.service.ts + shared.module.ts:22-25 | **THE API SENDS NO LOGGED ERROR TO SENTRY, AND THE SPEC THAT WOULD CATCH THAT TESTS AN ORPHAN.** There are TWO classes named `LoggerService`. (a) `logging/logger.interface.ts` — an `abstract class`, which is what `shared.module.ts` binds (`{provide: LoggerService, useExisting: WinstonLoggerService}`), what `shared/index.ts` re-exports, and what every service injects. (b) `logging/logger.service.ts` — a `@Injectable()` CONCRETE class carrying `captureToSentry`, whose header states "everything the codebase considers an error-level event ... flows through this one method, so Sentry capture lives here and nowhere else." Nothing imports (b) except its own spec. The DI-wired logger is `WinstonLoggerService`, which extends (a) and has NO Sentry code at all. F407 | api-core | apps/api/src/shared/logging/logging.interceptor.ts:150-178 vs src/shared/filters/global-exception.filter.ts:186-222 | **EVERY FAILED REQUEST IS LOGGED TWICE, AND THE INTERCEPTOR'S COPY IGNORES THE BY-STATUS LAW THE FILTER ENFORCES.** `LoggingInterceptor`'s `error` subscriber calls `this.logger.error(...)` for ANY exception, then the same exception reaches `GlobalExceptionFilter`, which logs it again. Bedrock: there is exactly one place that knows an exception's HTTP status, and it is the exception filter; an interceptor that fires before status resolution cannot classify severity and should not try. Rederive: delete `logError` from the interceptor and its `error` subscriber's logging (keep the `subscriber.error(error)` propagation); the filter remains the sole error logger, already correctly levelled and already carrying correlationId/userId. RED PROOF: re-adding a `this.logger.error(...)` to the error subscriber turns it RED ('Expected number of calls: 0, Received number of calls: 1'). Restored → green. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F416 | api-core | apps/api/src/shared/logging/winston-logger.service.ts:200-215 + logging.interceptor.ts:190-232 | **THE LOG REDACTION IS EXACT-KEY-MATCH, AND REQUEST BODIES ARE LOGGED WHOLESALE.** `sanitizeMetadata` redacts a key only when it equals one of `password/token/secret/key/authorization/cookie/session` exactly — so `apiKey`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `clientSecret`, `webhookSecret`, `sessionId` all pass through verbatim, and the codebase uses those spellings throughout its config. F479 | public-crave-score.service.ts writeScores | THE SCALE NOTE WAS RIGHT, AND THE CEILING IS HEAP, NOT SECONDS. rebuildAllScores scores the WHOLE graph in one run, so `scored.length` IS the corpus (24,032 subjects on the mirror), and the write built one `$executeRaw` per subject and handed the whole array to `$transaction`. MEASURED on the mirror against a clone of the real table: 24,032 subjects = 2,229 ms per-row vs 643 ms set-based; at 10x (240,320 subjects) = 18,610 ms / **2,461 MB heap** vs 5,251 ms / 790 MB. 2.4 GB of retained statement objects inside one transaction is an OOM on any container we run, reached by corpus growth alone — this is a real ceiling, not a micro-optimisation. | REDERIVED (2026-08-03): ONE `INSERT … SELECT … FROM unnest(...)` upsert; columns travel as parallel arrays. Numerics are bound as **text** and cast `::numeric` deliberately — the columns are `numeric(p,s)` and binding a float64 would re-round on top of the rounding scoreCandidates already did; `String(n)` is the shortest round-trip decimal and `::numeric` parses it exactly. The stale-subject prune stays a second statement in the SAME `$transaction`, so atomicity is unchanged. A NEW PRECONDITION IS NAMED, NOT ASSUMED: the per-row loop silently let a duplicated subject overwrite itself, whereas a set-based upsert raises Postgres' opaque "ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time" — distinctness is structural (loadCandidates builds both lists by iterating Maps keyed by connectionId/restaurantId, subjectType separating them), so a duplicate means that construction broke upstream, and writeScores now refuses by name. | FIXED | PROOF: (a) EQUIVALENCE, byte-level — both shapes fed the identical 24,032 live subjects into two clones of the real table; symmetric difference across all 11 written columns = **0 rows**. F804 | mobile-app-core | src/services/api.ts:304-383 | **THE ONE CLIENT HAS NO 401 SEAM.** The response interceptor handles 403+ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED and >=500, and nothing else. A 401 (expired/revoked Clerk session, or `getAuthToken` returning null because the token resolver threw — :265-271 swallows that into `logger.warn` + null) falls through to the generic failure modal, and the app keeps making unauthenticated requests forever with no sign-out and no re-auth prompt. The AuthProvider's resolver is the only refresh path and it has no retry. A 401 announces through `useSessionLapseStore` (mirroring entitlementLapseStore), tags the error `isSessionLapse`, and AppRouteCoordinator makes the SERVER's verdict win over Clerk's cached `isSignedIn`: authStatus becomes 'signed_out', the react-query cache is cleared, and the route is sign-in. Silent-anonymous is no longer representable. The lapse clears on a real session change (signed out, or a new user id). MUTATION-PROVED: api-failure-policy.spec.ts, 8 pass, incl. 'THE TRANSITION: a 401 flips the app into an explicit signed-out state'; deleting the `status === 401` case fails 2 cases including the store transition | read the whole interceptor + AuthProvider token resolver | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

### errors that reach nobody

F810 | mobile-app-core | src/screens/Onboarding.tsx:451-463 | **SILENT LOSS OF THE ONE THING ONBOARDING EXISTS TO COLLECT.** When the user is signed in and `usersService.completeOnboarding` throws, the catch logs a warn, CLEARS the service-issue banner (`clearServiceIssue('global')` — actively hiding the evidence), and marks onboarding complete LOCALLY. The persisted status is now `completed`, so the flow never runs again and the payload — every answer, plus the username claim — is never retried or replayed. The user believes they finished; the server has nothing. There is no outbox and no reconciliation on next launch. LADDER — compensates-for: a real fear, that a network blip strands a user on the last onboarding screen. bedrock: the answers are the product's cold-start signal; losing them silently is worse than a retry. rederive: complete locally AND enqueue the payload for replay (the answers already live in the persisted zustand draft — keep the draft until the server confirms, and re-send on next authenticated launch). What becomes impossible: a completed-locally user whose answers never landed. | keep the draft until server-confirmed; replay on launch | FIXED (D38) — the answers are DURABLE DATA (owner, 2026-08-03) and can no longer be discarded. The catch no longer clears the service-issue banner and no longer marks onboarding complete: it records the exact rejected payload in a PERSISTED outbox (`onboardingStore.pendingServerCompletion`, in `partialize` so it survives a cold start), surfaces the failure through `completionError` (the CTA stays live, so pressing it again retries), and returns false. AppRouteCoordinator replays the payload on the next authenticated launch via `decideOnboardingCompletionReplay`; only a CONFIRMED server write empties the outbox, and it NEVER expires — a payload we cannot land today is still the only copy of the user's answers. RED-PROVED: onboarding-completion-replay.spec.ts drives the REAL persisted store through a REAL failing call, 8 pass; restoring the old catch (completeOnboardingLocally + return true) fails 4, including 'RED — a failing server call does NOT mark onboarding complete' and 'the payload survives VERBATIM, username claim included' | read completeAndEnterApp + onboardingStore.completeOnboardingLocally | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

(2) THE OTHER LEAK, found while fixing this one and NOT in the finding: the transition engine's join-liveness watchdog was never disarmed when a txn left 'joining', so every transition left a live 600ms timer — that was what force-killed the worker in the full run. `advance`/`supersede` now disarm it, `resetTransitionTxnHolderForTest` disarms every armed watchdog (a txn a spec created directly was never in the holder), and the spec calls it in afterEach. (3) THE GATE: `yarn test` now runs `scripts/jest-honest.js`, which streams jest's output and FAILS the run on 'A worker process has failed to exit gracefully', 'A worker process has crashed', 'Cannot log after tests are done', and the force-exit notices. RED-PROVED: with the watchdog leak present, jest exits 0 while the runner exits 1 naming the marker (captured run: 53 suites / 486 tests 'passed', 12 post-teardown logs, jest exit 0, runner exit 1). SURPRISE WORTH RECORDING: in-band (single-file) the crash DOES exit 1, but with 2+ suites the worker death is swallowed ENTIRELY — no message at all, exit 0. F759 | api-identity-money | apps/api/src/modules/billing/billing.service.ts, billing.controller.ts, dto/create-checkout-session.dto.ts, prisma/schema.prisma (CheckoutSession + checkout_session_status), migrations/20260803130000_restore_stripe_checkout_rail, config/configuration.ts (stripe.\*) | THE STRIPE WEB CHECKOUT RAIL WAS MISSING FOR THE PLAN THAT NOW DEPENDS ON IT. Deleted 2026-07-09 in c2861853 under the then-true rationale "models a rail that doesn't exist"; owner ruled 2026-08-01/08-03 that web checkout IS the plan (Strava dual-button paywall, ~97% net vs ~85% via StoreKit, Apple-commission-free out-of-app under the April 2025 Epic contempt ruling). Without it the primary paywall button had no URL to open. | RESTORED where the old shape was still right (hosted Checkout session creation, the attempt-log table, the portal session, `checkout.session.completed`). RE-DERIVED onto today's tree where it was not: (1) the DTO no longer accepts client `successUrl`/`cancelUrl` — an open redirect wearing a feature's clothes; all three redirect URLs plus the price id come from config with NO defaults (no-fake-estimates: a guessed price sells the wrong thing, a guessed redirect strands a payer), and an unconfigured rail 503s naming the missing env vars. (2) SINGLE-PRODUCT LAW is now enforced on BOTH doors: a `priceId` that is not the configured premium price is a 400 naming both ids, and a subscription arriving with an `entitlement_code` outside the closed ledger vocabulary throws (event recorded FAILED + replayable) instead of minting a paid grant under a code `accessVerdict()` never asks about — the same D1-residual hole `RevenueCatEntitlementMap` refuses at boot, closed on the Stripe side. (3) ENTITLEMENTS UNIFY THROUGH THE ACCESS-GRANT LEDGER, not the restored table: `checkout.session.completed` retrieves the subscription and funnels into the same `syncSubscriptionGrant` the subscription events use, idempotent per `stripe:<subId>`, so whichever of the two events Stripe delivers first is sufficient and the second is a no-op. The table is the ATTEMPT log only. (4) `subscription_data.metadata` is stamped at session creation — Stripe does NOT copy Checkout Session metadata onto the subscription, so without it every web subscription event would log "without matching user" and grant nothing. (5) `ensureStripeCustomer` came back into BillingService rather than UserService: it is billing's business and nothing else ever called it. (6) The recreated table is timestamptz throughout and FK RESTRICT, per the laws that postdate its deletion. | FIXED (2026-08-03) | PROOF: `npx jest billing entitlements` 86/86 green (12 new in billing-checkout.spec.ts, stripe SDK mocked — zero live vendor calls); `yarn build` clean; migration applied locally and `prisma migrate diff` shows ZERO checkout drift. **AMENDED 2026-08-03 (same day, owner ruling): TWO PRICES OF THE ONE PRODUCT, and the single-product law got STRONGER, not looser.** The owner ruled that the web paywall shows the SAME structure as the in-app one (Strava pattern: same offers, different payment location) — $7.99/mo and $39.99/yr with an annual-only ~1-week free trial. So `stripe.premiumPriceId` (STRIPE_PREMIUM_PRICE_ID) became the closed pair `stripe.prices.{monthly,annual}` (STRIPE_MONTHLY_PRICE_ID / STRIPE_ANNUAL_PRICE_ID), and the DTO's `priceId` field was DELETED in favour of `{ plan: 'monthly' | 'annual' }`. Note what this does to the law: the original shape enforced 'premium is the only product' by comparing a client-supplied opaque Stripe id against the configured one — a refusal. A two-word vocabulary makes a price id outside the configured pair UNREPRESENTABLE, because the caller cannot name a price at all; the api alone maps word -> price. One PRODUCT, two PRICES of it; `entitlement_code` metadata is identical on both plans, so both grant the same thing `accessVerdict()` asks about. `plan` is REQUIRED, never defaulted — a paywall showing two prices against a body that silently means 'monthly' is a charge the user did not pick. The trial lives in the SESSION (`subscription_data.trial_period_days = ANNUAL_TRIAL_PERIOD_DAYS = 7`, annual only, spread in rather than set-to-undefined) not on the Stripe price, so the offer the copy promises and the offer the code builds are the same object. `requireCheckoutConfig()` requires BOTH prices regardless of the requested plan: a half-configured rail must 503 on the FIRST request, not on the unlucky user who picks the other button. PROOF: `npx jest billing --silent` 53/53 green; `yarn build` clean; zero live vendor calls (stripe SDK still mocked wholesale). F760 | site + api-identity-money | apps/site/** (new workspace: src/config.ts, src/clerk-frontend-api.ts, src/premium-page.ts, src/router.ts, src/server.ts, src/pages/{index,privacy,terms,support}.html, test/router.test.ts, Dockerfile, README.md, package.json, tsconfig.json), railway.site.json, apps/api/src/main.ts (CORS) | THE PUBLIC WEBSITE HAD NO SOURCE. craveapp.ai was a Railway bun "function" whose ENTIRE source was a base64 blob inside the service's `startCommand` — four HTML constants and an if-chain, outside the repo, outside git, outside review, un-diffable and un-testable. D39 ruled it must carry web payments (Strava dual-button, ~97% net); that shape cannot hold auth or checkout at all. SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT FOUND WHILE WIRING IT: prod CORS was a flat `origin: false`. Correct while the only client was the native app (not a browser, sends no Origin) — but it makes the browser's POST /billing/checkout-session unreachable, so F759's restored rail had a URL nobody could ask for. The web rail was DEAD ON ARRIVAL in prod and nothing said so. | REDERIVED as apps/site, a zero-dependency node:http server (runs unchanged on Bun; node:http chosen over Bun.serve so the shipped server is the one the tests exercise — bun is not installed on the dev machine, and a test that cannot run is not a test). (1) The four pages are PRESERVED, captured from the live site, with exactly one edit: Cloudflare had rewritten every support@craveapp.ai link into `__cf_email__` obfuscation that renders only if a CDN script loads — those are plain mailto: links again, and a test asserts no cdn-cgi/**cf_email** residue survives. (2) /premium: Clerk sign-in for the SAME instance as the app, then a JWT-TEMPLATE bearer to `${API_ORIGIN}/api/v1/billing/checkout-session` with an EMPTY body, then follow the returned hosted-Stripe url. Empty body is the point: the site names no price (single-product law is the api's to enforce) and no redirect URL (the DTO stopped accepting client successUrl/cancelUrl — an open redirect wearing a feature's clothes); /premium/success and /premium/cancelled exist to BE the configured STRIPE*CHECKOUT*\*\_URL targets, not to be passed as them. Tests assert /priceId/ and /successUrl|cancelUrl/ NEVER appear in the served page. (3) The Clerk frontend-API host is DERIVED from the publishable key (which is base64 of that host) rather than being a fourth env var — a hand-typed host that disagrees with the key signs visitors into the wrong Clerk instance and the api then rejects every token; a malformed key throws naming the reason instead of guessing, including a hostname-shape check so a corrupt key cannot inject a path into the script src. (4) NO SECRET LIVES HERE: no Stripe key, no Clerk secret key, no DB URL. Env contract is three non-secret vars (API_ORIGIN, CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, PORT=8080) plus CLERK_JWT_TEMPLATE. (5) An unconfigured checkout is an OUTAGE and must look like one: /premium answers 503 naming the missing vars, while the four static pages keep serving — a billing misconfiguration must never take the Privacy Policy offline. (6) api CORS now reads WEB_ORIGIN (comma-separated exact origins) and, UNSET, leaves prod EXACTLY as strict as before — an allowlist, not a loosening, and a config-less deploy changes nothing. credentials stays false (bearer header, never a cookie). | FIXED (2026-08-03) | PROOF: 12/12 `node --test` green in apps/site; root `yarn build` green (4/4 turbo tasks, site included). MUTATION-PROVEN RED: changing /premium's unconfigured status 503->200 and dropping the trailing-slash normalization turns exactly 2 tests red ("/premium is 503 (not a broken 200) when unconfigured", "trailing slashes and case do not 302 a real page away"); restored, 12/12 green. ZERO VENDOR CALLS in tests (the fixture publishable key is base64 of "fake-clerk.example.com$"). NOT DONE (out of scope, reported): nothing staged, committed, or deployed; Railway untouched; the base64-startCommand function is still the live site until the owner executes the cutover in apps/site/README.md. **AMENDED 2026-08-03 (owner ruling, paired with F759's amendment): /premium NOW SHOWS BOTH OFFERS.\*\* The page shipped with a single 'Continue to secure checkout' button posting an empty body — which, once the api grew two prices, would have quietly steered every web buyer onto whichever price the api happened to pick as the default. The Strava pattern is the SAME offers in a different payment location, not a reduced menu, so /premium renders two plan cards in the existing dark/light visual language: $7.99/mo (Cancel anytime) and $39.99/yr (1 week free, then $39.99/year), each button posting `{"plan":"…"}` built from its own `data-plan`. The 'never names a price' property SURVIVES and is now structural: the page cannot express a Stripe price id, only a plan word. HONEST COPY IS TESTED, not just present — the annual note must say what happens AFTER the trial ('1 week free, then $39.99/year'); '1 week free' alone is the half-truth that produces chargebacks — and a test asserts the trial is never promised on monthly. The dollar amounts and the trial length are COPY, not configuration: they must match the Stripe prices and ANNUAL_TRIAL_PERIOD_DAYS, and the README says so, because only the api can charge — a mismatch is a LIE ON THE PAGE, not a wrong charge, which is worse rather than better. Both buttons disable together while either is in flight (one impatient double-click must not open two payment pages for one decision). Still zero dependencies, zero secrets, zero vendor calls. PROOF: `yarn workspace site build` + `test` 13/13 green. MUTATION-PROVEN RED: (d) hard-coding the POST body to `{"plan":"monthly"}` (ignoring the button) = 1 red; (e) deleting the annual offer card = 2 red; restored, 13/13 green. OPEN DEPENDENCY: CLERK_JWT_TEMPLATE defaults to 'mobile' because that is the ONLY template known to mint an audience CLERK_JWT_AUDIENCE accepts — a dedicated 'web' template requires adding its aud to the api first, or every checkout 401s. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F958 | mobile-nav-overlays | apps/mobile/src/navigation/runtime/route-scene-layout-_.ts (7 files) + route-sheet-_-state-controller.ts (6 files), ~1,400 lines | ABSTRACTION APPLIED PAST THE POINT THE CONCEPTS ARE DISTINCT. A projection pipeline in which most stages project a value onto ITSELF: `nav-frame -> search-bar-frame -> frame -> shell -> (snap-points -> sheet) -> layout` is seven controllers, each with its own `Set<Listener>`, `dispose`, memoized `recompute(notify)` and `are*Equal` — and `RouteSceneLayoutShellSnapshot` is FIELD-IDENTICAL to `RouteSceneLayoutFrameSnapshot` (route-scene-layout-shell-state-controller.ts:6-9 vs route-scene-layout-frame-state-controller.ts:13-16), while `RouteSceneLayoutSheetSnapshot` is a one-field wrapper around `snapPoints`. Same story for the five `route-sheet-{chrome-geometry,chrome-motion,chrome-visual,presentation,visual}` controllers. The whole family assembles TWO composite values (`SearchRouteSceneLayoutState`, `SearchRouteSheetVisualSelectionSnapshot`) from two source authorities. Ladder: compensates-for = a real past problem (one giant recompute re-notifying everyone); bedrock = a controller exists per INDEPENDENTLY-CHANGING fact; rederive = collapse to one controller per source authority with derived selectors, keeping the two composite outputs byte-identical. This is the territory's largest structural cleanup and the one that most wants an owner decision before anyone touches it. | ESCALATED (design; large) | read all 13 | STATUS: ESCALATED | TRIAGE (2026-08-05, bucket b/OWNER'S — REWRITTEN FOR A ONE-SITTING ANSWER): QUESTION: runtime/navigation's route-scene-layout-_/route-sheet-_-state-controller family is 13 files, ~1,400 lines, of near-duplicate projection controllers (RouteSceneLayoutShellSnapshot is field-identical to RouteSceneLayoutFrameSnapshot; one field is copied unchanged through 5 controller hops). Is collapsing this to one controller per independently-changing source authority worth the risk of a large refactor on a shipped, high-traffic surface? OPTIONS: (1) Do the collapse now — the row proposes createDerivedSnapshotAuthority({sources, project, isEqual}) as the shared seam, keeping the two composite outputs byte-identical. (2) Defer — leave the duplication as documented technical debt; it's correct today, just costly to maintain (two of this pass's bugs, F1052f and F1061, trace to hand-written comparators in exactly this family). RECOMMENDATION: defer until a concrete need forces a touch (e.g., the next bug in this family) — it's the largest, riskiest refactor in the ledger with no user-visible payoff on its own, and per CLAUDE.md's testing methodology a structural change to a shipped surface wants its own scoped verification pass, not a residue-drain edit. COST: ~1,400 lines touched across 13 files if done now; zero cost to defer beyond the ongoing bug-density this family produces. NEXT ACTION: send the QUESTION above to the owner for a one-sitting decision (options + recommendation + cost already laid out); no code change until they rule.

Its headline recommendation is `useKeyedCallback` / `useCallbackFactory` for list-item callback stability ("GOOD: Returns stable references keyed by ID"). Repo-wide grep: BOTH symbols appear only in their own definition file (hooks/useCallbackFactory.ts) and the barrel re-export — not one consumer anywhere in apps/mobile/src. F1037 | mobile-search | runtime/shared/search-open-now-projection.ts | IDEAL-VERIFIED on the single most-suspected client-re-derivation in the territory — and the suspicion was WRONG, recorded so the next pass does not re-hunt it. "Open now" is NOT recomputed client-side: the projection FILTERS on the server-provided `operatingStatus.isOpen` (rows) and the API's per-feature `isOpen` (coverage). It never parses an hours string and never consults the device clock. Three things make it exemplary: (1) rows WITHOUT openness data are DROPPED, explicitly "matching the server's open-now post-filter semantics exactly" — the client mirrors server semantics rather than inventing gentler ones; (2) `coverageCarriesOpenness` is a real VERSION-SKEW guard that can fail — an older API omitting `isOpen` would silently empty the coverage, so the projection DECLINES instead of producing a confidently-wrong empty map; (3) the projected totals are marked PROVISIONAL in the metadata and the resolver settles them with the honest server slice as a version update (no second reveal), so the optimistic paint can never harden into a wrong number. This is the correct shape for optimistic client projection of a server truth, and it is the counter-example that isolates F1018/F1019: the re-derivation disease in this territory is NOT in the runtime layer, it is confined to the components/utils layer. | IDEAL-VERIFIED | full read + compared against the server's open-now post-filter | STATUS: MOOT (was: IDEAL-VERIFIED)

F1101 | mobile-native | apps/mobile/ios/cravesearch/cravesearch.entitlements:1-8 (whole file) + apps/mobile/src/providers/AuthProvider.tsx:226 | THE ENTITLEMENTS FILE HARDCODES `aps-environment = development` AND NOTHING ELSE, while the app really does register for push: `Notifications.getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` runs in AuthProvider, and `src/services/push-permission.ts:79` requests the OS permission. `aps-environment` selects WHICH APNs the token is minted against — `development` = the sandbox gateway. Failure scenario: a TestFlight/App Store build carrying this value mints sandbox tokens; the api pushes to production APNs; every notification silently disappears with no client-visible error (BadDeviceToken server-side at most). This is the classic "push works on my sim, dies in TestFlight" bug, and it is invisible until real users are on the build. Caveat kept honest: EAS's managed-credential flow can rewrite the entitlement at archive time from the provisioning profile, so this MAY be masked in practice — but the repo cannot prove that, and `eas.json` has no ios credentials block. Ladder: the value is the Expo prebuild default for a dev-only app; it compensated for "we only ever ran a dev client". Bedrock = the entitlement is `$(APS_ENVIRONMENT)` driven per-configuration (development for Debug, production for Release), so the shipped value is a consequence of the build, not a constant. | **RESOLVED-AS-NON-DEFECT (2026-08-03), + instrument added.** MECHANISM (proved from installed source, not plausibility): the APNs environment is chosen from the EMBEDDED PROVISIONING PROFILE at runtime, never from this file. `node_modules/expo-notifications/build/getExpoPushTokenAsync.js:60` sets the request's `development` flag from `shouldUseDevelopmentNotificationService()` (:150-160), which calls `Application.getIosPushNotificationServiceEnvironmentAsync()`; that resolves in `node_modules/expo-application/ios/EXApplication/EXProvisioningProfile.m:28-36` by reading `Entitlements["aps-environment"]` out of the bundle's `embedded.mobileprovision`. Expo's push service therefore routes each token to sandbox/production by what the SIGNED PROFILE says. A store profile (eas.json `production`: `"distribution": "store"`, no `credentialsSource` ⇒ EAS remote managed credentials mint an App Store distribution profile) and an ad-hoc profile both carry `production`; only development-signed builds carry `development`. Xcode's packaging step independently substitutes the profile's aps-environment into the signed `.xcent`, so the compiled literal here is not what ships either. `app.json:43-45` mirrors the same dev value and is equally inert (the ios/ project is authoritative and is not prebuilt). NO CODE FIX NEEDED — the entitlements comment now states why `development` is correct. INSTRUMENT (so the next TestFlight build proves itself): `reportPushEnvironmentClassification()` in `apps/mobile/src/providers/AuthProvider.tsx` runs before every `getExpoPushTokenAsync`, logs `[PushEnv] apsEnvironment=… releaseType=…`, and fires `captureHandledError` (Sentry, seam `push:aps-environment`) ONLY on the genuinely broken combination — a distributed build (APP_STORE/TestFlight, AD_HOC, ENTERPRISE) reporting a non-production APNs environment. It can show RED. `expo-application` promoted from transitive to a direct dep (`~7.0.8`, already pod-linked via expo-notifications). So: a dependency is paid for, a channel is configured, a check-on-launch policy is set, and none of it can ever run. Failure scenario: someone ships a hotfix expecting OTA delivery and it never reaches a device; or updates get flipped on and the stale `EXUpdatesSDKVersion` makes the server serve the wrong manifest. Ladder: `EXUpdatesEnabled=false` is the honest current state (no OTA); the channels and the stale SDK version are the residue. Is OTA a distribution lane the app wants, or not? OPTIONS: (1) ENABLE it — fix EXUpdatesSDKVersion to match the real Expo SDK, wire Updates.checkForUpdateAsync deliberately, use the channels that are already configured. (2) DROP it — remove expo-updates, the channel keys in eas.json, and Expo.plist's dead update keys. RECOMMENDATION: none — this is a genuine roadmap call (does hotfix-without-app-store-review matter to the release cadence this app wants) that this pass should not make unilaterally; the incoherence itself (stale SDK version, configured-but-inert channels) is a defect either way and should be cleaned up regardless of which way the owner rules. COST: (1) = ongoing OTA infra + testing; (2) = removes a paid dependency and simplifies eas.json, near-zero cost since nothing uses it today. NEXT ACTION: send the QUESTION above to the owner for a one-sitting decision (options + recommendation + cost already laid out); no code change until they rule.

F1106 | mobile-native | apps/mobile/ios/cravesearch/Info.plist (3 location keys) vs apps/mobile/src | OVER-DECLARED LOCATION PERMISSIONS. Info.plist declares all three of `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`, `NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription` and `NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription`, all with the same generic string "Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to access your location". But the app never asks for Always/background: repo-wide grep of `src/` for `requestBackgroundPermissionsAsync` and `startLocationUpdatesAsync` returns ZERO, there is no `UIBackgroundModes` key, and no location background entitlement. Failure scenario: App Store review treats declared Always-usage as an intent to track in the background and asks why, or worse the reviewer sees a purpose string that does not describe a real feature — a rejection class that costs a full review cycle. Secondary: the string itself is the template default and explains no benefit to the user, which measurably depresses grant rates on the one permission this product cannot function without. Ladder: template default. F1107 | mobile-native | apps/mobile/ios/cravesearch/Info.plist (no NSPhotoLibrary\* key) vs apps/mobile/src/overlays/PostPhotosFunnelHost.tsx:119 | NO `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` / `NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription` ANYWHERE, while `ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync(...)` IS called on the post-photos path. Honest nuance, stated so this is not overclaimed: expo-image-picker 17 goes through `PHPickerViewController` by default, which is out-of-process and needs NO permission and NO usage string — and the code never calls `requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync`, which is consistent with the PHPicker path. So this is very likely NOT a runtime crash today. It IS a live risk on two edges: (a) any option change that drops to the legacy library path, or any future save-to-camera-roll, crashes instantly on a missing usage string — the single most common iOS launch-blocker; (b) Apple's binary analysis flags linked photo-library APIs with no declared purpose. Ladder: the key was never needed because PHPicker was always the path. Ladder: the bridge modules predate the new-arch flip; the interop layer compensates. Is migrating the native boundary to real TurboModules/codegen worth scheduling? OPTIONS: (1) Migrate incrementally — start with the highest-payload boundaries (SearchChromeScalarSurfaceRegistry's 10 methods, the render controller's 11), explicitly AFTER the map is untouched-stable per the row's own sequencing note (map is owner-locked). (2) Leave as-is — the interop layer works today (the app ships), this is strategic debt, not a live bug. RECOMMENDATION: defer until there's a concrete driver (e.g., a recurring signature-drift bug) — MapLodKit already proves the model (typed pure core + 41 tests, no simulator needed) as a template for when the migration does happen, so nothing is lost by waiting. COST: large, multi-module migration; deferring costs nothing beyond continued exposure to F1112's signature-drift class.

(2) UIUserInterfaceStyle='Light' force-locks the whole app out of dark mode, plausibly deliberate (map/labels tuned for a light basemap) but nowhere stated as intentional.
