(2) Either state the light-mode lock as a deliberate decision (a comment + a CLAUDE.md line, so it survives) or unlock dark mode. RECOMMENDATION: (1) rename before any store submission — this is close to a launch-blocker, not a nice-to-have; low cost. (2) state the decision in writing regardless of which way the owner rules — it costs one comment and prevents a future engineer from 'fixing' an intentional lock. COST: (1) = one-line app.json/plist change; (2) = documentation only, or a real dark-theme project if reversed (large, undertaken separately).

F1117 | mobile-native | apps/mobile/ios/Podfile.lock + absence of any Mapbox download credential in the repo or ~/.netrc | `pod install` IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE ON A CLEAN MACHINE. Mapbox's iOS SDK ships from a private maven/CocoaPods endpoint that requires a secret download token, conventionally in `~/.netrc`. Verified: no `~/.netrc` on this machine, and no `MAPBOX_DOWNLOADS_TOKEN`/`MGLMapboxAccessToken`/netrc reference in the Podfile, in `apps/mobile/android/gradle.properties`, or anywhere in the tree. Podfile.lock nonetheless pins MapboxMaps 11.26.0-rc.1 with checksums — so the pods were fetched once, and the working setup depends on a locally cached `Pods/` directory plus a credential nobody has written down. Failure scenario: a fresh clone, a new machine, an EAS build worker, or anyone who runs `pod deintegrate` gets a 401 from Mapbox with no documented recovery — and the failure will read as "the map dependency is broken", not "you are missing a credential". Same class as the Android token gap in F1110, one platform over. Related but separate and NOT a defect: the runtime PUBLIC access token is correctly set from JS (`MapboxGL.setAccessToken` at `src/screens/Search/runtime/shared/use-search-root-map-bootstrap-runtime.ts:52` and `src/components/BackdropMapScene.tsx:36`) rather than baked into Info.plist — that is the right shape. Ladder: the token was typed into a machine once. F1055 | mobile-search | runtime/profile/profile-app-foreground-runtime.ts:36-45 + profile-close-state-record.ts:55-66 + profile-close-foreground-runtime-state.ts:24-27 | A WRITE-ONLY RESTORE LEDGER — the profile open HIDES the save sheet and nothing ever puts it back. `prepareForegroundUiForProfileOpen({captureSaveSheetState:true})` reads the live `saveSheetState`, sets `visible:false`, and RETURNS the previous state; `executeProfileOpenPresentationPlan` (profile-open-action-execution.ts:60) hands it to `capturePreviousForegroundUiRestoreStateIfAbsent`, which stores it on `controllerState.runtime.close.previousForegroundUiRestoreState`. The reader `getPreviousForegroundUiRestoreState` is defined, exported on `ProfileCloseForegroundRuntimeState`, and CALLED BY NOBODY — repo-wide `grep -rn "getPreviousForegroundUiRestoreState" apps/mobile/src` returns only its own definition/type/memo-dep lines, and `grep -rn "setSaveSheetState" apps/mobile/src` shows the ONLY writer outside the overlay controller is the hide at profile-app-foreground-runtime.ts:39. `finalizePreparedProfileCloseRecord` then nulls the field on close. So: open a restaurant profile with the save sheet up → the sheet is dismissed, the state to restore it is captured, and it is discarded at close. It does NOT enumerate `messages.shared_entity_id` — a user sharing a restaurant or dish into a DM (`kind='entity_share'`, `shared_entity_kind` in {restaurant,dish}, the id a bare core_entities uuid resolved through SaveableEntityResolver). The column is `text` with no FK, so nothing else catches it either. The redirect hop cannot rescue it: share-package-resolver.service.ts:150-153 added that hop precisely so a MERGED restaurant stays resolvable, and a wipe DELETES rather than merges, so no redirect row exists. Note the near-miss that makes this a real gap rather than a theoretical one: `user_taste_profile.subject_id` (new 2026-08-03) is also unenumerated but is safe by derivation — it is a projection of `signals`, which IS anchored. Messages are not derived from anything. | LADDER: compensates for the anchor set being an enumeration written when messaging did not exist, in a file whose OWN header calls itself "THE canonical user-anchor set (single source of truth)". An enumeration cannot be a single source of truth for a growing schema — this is the `filesImporting()` disease in SQL. Bedrock: "user data points at this entity" is a property derivable from the SCHEMA (every column, declared-FK or not, that stores a core_entities id and lives in a user-layer table), not from a list someone maintains. Rederive: a spec that reads information_schema, enumerates every uuid/text column in the user layer, and FAILS on any column not either present in preserved-anchors.sql or explicitly listed as derived-and-therefore-covered (with the covering surface named) — so the next `messages` fails a test instead of failing a user. F1254 | api-scripts | apps/api/scripts/validate-crave-score-fixtures.ts:50, 686-696 vs rescore-coordinator.service.ts:46-103 | **A SCRIPT NAMED "validate…fixtures" RUNS AN UNLOCKED GLOBAL SCORE REBUILD BY DEFAULT.** §12.6 is explicit and `rebuild-crave-scores.ts` obeys it verbatim in its own docstring: "global rebuilds happen ONLY through the singleton rescorer" — advisory-locked (`pg_try_advisory_lock(0x63726176)`), flag cleared before the rebuild, re-dirtied on failure, driven hourly by `@Cron(EVERY_HOUR)`. In `src/` that law holds perfectly: `RescoreCoordinatorService:80` is the ONLY caller of `rebuildAllScores()`. The second caller in the whole tree is this script, at line 696, calling `scorer.rebuildAllScores()` directly — no lock, no dirty flag, no coordinator. And it is the DEFAULT path: the escape is `--skip-db`, i.e. opt-OUT. Against any database where crons run, an operator "validating fixtures" races the hourly rebuild; two concurrent global rebuilds over the same subject table is exactly what the advisory lock was installed to make impossible. Note the corpus already knows the right polarity — wipe-city-derived.sql's own closing comment reasons about opt-in vs opt-out and picks opt-IN (`-v execute=1`) for the routine sweep. | LADDER: compensates for wanting a smoke check on real data without the ceremony. Bedrock: if a service owns an operation under a lock, the lock IS the operation's entry point; a script that reaches past it has forked the authority. Rederive: the script drives the COORDINATOR (mark dirty + one tick), exactly as rebuild-crave-scores.ts does — same code path, lock included — and the DB leg becomes opt-in (`--with-db`) so the in-memory invariant suite, which is the part that belongs in a fixture validator, is what a bare invocation runs. F1256 | api-scripts | apps/api/scripts/seed-google-photos.ts:106-118, 129 | **BILLED GOOGLE PLACES CALLS THAT NEVER REACH THE METER.** The seeder calls Places Details (`/places/{id}?fields=photos.name`) and Places Photo Media (`/{photoName}/media`) with a raw `fetch` and a bare `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`, bypassing the vendor client, the rate-limit coordinator, the durable spend pool and `api_usage_ledger` entirely — 8 photos per restaurant across a default 15 top-Austin restaurants plus every restaurant in the owner's favorite lists. Both endpoints are billed SKUs. This is small money, and that is exactly what makes it a measurement defect rather than a spend defect: the cost-truth law's whole method is billed-vs-ledger reconciliation, and unmetered vendor calls land in the BigQuery export with no ledger counterpart, where they are indistinguishable from — and get absorbed into — the known ~1.7x under-metering. `publish-reconciliation.ts` then bakes that contamination into a durable per-vendor multiplier in `spend_unit_costs`, which `prepareManifestEstimate` multiplies every future estimate by. A dev-fixture script therefore biases the owner-facing cost manifest. The one-off-cost lesson recorded twice in CLAUDE.md (the $118 line, then the $0.028→$0.045 correction) is the same error one level up: summing a source that does not contain all the spend. | LADDER: compensates for a fixture seeder not wanting to boot the Nest graph to get a vendor client. Bedrock: there is one gateway per vendor and it meters — a raw `fetch` to a billed host is the gateway law violated, whoever the caller is. Rederive: the seeder acquires the metered Places client the same way any consumer does, or (if staying standalone is worth it) writes its own `api_usage_ledger` rows through the shared pricer, so ledger-vs-billed stays an honest comparison. Red team: check the rest of the corpus for the same shape before fixing one instance — `data-fixes/audit-catalog-vs-vendor.ts:64` and `data-fixes/resolve-entity-names.ts:69` raw-fetch TomTom identically; TomTom is quota-priced rather than per-call so the spend consequence differs, but the metering hole is the same. | **FIXED (D47, 2026-08-03).** The seeder boots the graph (with `stopCronsForScript`) purely to obtain `GooglePlacesService`, and both billed calls go through it. Place Details rides the existing metered path. Photo Media had NO metered path at all, so one was built: `getPlacePhotoUri()` with the same dollar-gate-then-rate-gate order and an `api_usage_ledger` row; `photoMedia` joins `PlacesOperation` (compile-enforced, so its rate limits could not be forgotten) at 7,000 µUSD/call. Red-team item honoured: the two TomTom raw-fetch siblings are named in the file's own header as the same shape still open. | **PROOF:** `grep -rn "placesCostMicrosPerCall"` → priced only in usage-ledger.service.ts / spend-analytics / vendor-pricing and the two cost scripts; seed-google-photos.ts appears nowhere in the metering path, and its only vendor plumbing is `PLACES_BASE` + two `fetch` calls + `process.env.GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`. **PROOF (executed, D47):** `tsc --noEmit` clean and the full suite green after the change; no vendor call was MADE (the seeder spends real money, so it was not run — the proof is structural: `grep` for raw `fetch` in seed-google-photos.ts returns nothing and `PLACES_BASE` is gone). **A SECOND UNDER-METER FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FIRST:** `photos` was absent from `ENTERPRISE_FIELDS`, so a `photos.name` details call would have classified as `essentials` (5,000 µUSD) instead of `enterprise` (20,000) — and `classifyPlacesSku` compared whole mask entries, so the sub-field `photos.name` would never have matched even once `photos` was added. Both fixed (top-level-field normalisation + the field added). Same disease one level down as the $118 and $0.028→$0.045 lessons: the classifier was never asked, because the only caller had bypassed it. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

F1257 | api-scripts | apps/api/src/modules/external-integrations/llm/llm.service.ts:449-466 (surfaced by every Nest-booting probe) | **A READ-ONLY PROBE MINTS A BILLED GEMINI CACHE AT BOOT — AND THE FIX FOR THIS EXACT BUG IS SITTING THREE LINES BELOW, APPLIED TO THE OTHER CACHE.** Running `corpus-integrity.ts` (a file whose docstring says "PURE read-only SQL against the live DB; no recall, no linker, no fixture") emitted, unprompted: `Creating explicit cache for system instructions … reason: bootstrap, systemPromptLength: 79513` then `System instruction cache created successfully … ttlSeconds: 10800` with a fresh cacheId — a ~20k-token context rented for three hours by a nine-second read-only query. Gemini cache STORAGE is billed in token-hours; `scripts/lib/cost-report.ts:319-323` documents this precisely, having already been burned by it ("cache-STORAGE rows price by token-hours, and without it they fell through to the cached-READ rate — 13 cents reported as 0.2 cents"). The registry's cross-process reuse mitigates but does not close it (my run paid a create). The same boot also WROTE durable pool state (`gemini.monthlySpend backstop re-derived from measured spend at boot, beforeUsd 475 → afterUsd 684.34`) from a script the corpus calls read-only. Both are module-init side effects: the containment lockdown stops the CRONS a script boot starts and nothing else, so "this script is read-only" is a claim about the script's own statements that its dependency graph quietly falsifies. | LADDER: compensates for the API path wanting a warm cache on the first request. AND THE LAW IS NAMED, next to `stopCronsForScript` as asked: _a script boot must not start billed or mutating background work_ — with the family enumerated (cron registration; query cache; system cache) and the one member still OPEN recorded in place (the spend pool's monthly-backstop re-derivation still writes durable state at module init) so it is not rediscovered as a surprise. Each member is closed at its own lazy seam rather than behind a script-mode flag, because the right owner of a cost-bearing resource is the consumer, not a mode the boot must remember to set. | **PROOF (executed):** full boot log of `npx ts-node -T scripts/search-harness/corpus-integrity.ts --json` captured; the cache-create and the pool re-derivation lines are quoted above verbatim from that run. llm.service.ts:451 `bootstrapSystemInstructionCache()` is called unconditionally from `onModuleInit`; :464-465 is the lazy-by-lesson comment on the sibling. **PROOF (executed, D47):** `npx ts-node -T scripts/search-harness/corpus-integrity.ts --json` re-run after the change — **zero** cache-create lines (`grep -icE 'explicit cache|System instruction cache created'` → 0), against the pass-2 boot log of the SAME command which emitted `Creating explicit cache for system instructions … reason: bootstrap, systemPromptLength: 79513` then `System instruction cache created successfully … ttlSeconds: 10800`. The RED side is that recorded log; it was deliberately not re-created, because re-creating it costs a real billed three-hour cache rental. | STATUS: FIXED (was: FIXED)

Contrast the file next door: `createResultsPresentationAuthority()`really does`new`per call. Consequences are latent rather than live today (one Search screen per process), but`reset()`is a process-global wipe, the diagnostics ring is shared across every mount, and a second Search host (or a test that mounts twice without resetting) silently shares state while the type system and the provider both say otherwise. F836 the `'data' in response.data` unwrap deleted — `listCitiesForList` is typed `Promise<Array<…>>` and returns a bare array, so `'data' in []` was always false. The `Array.isArray` check STAYS: that one can fail. F837 all three dead compatibility branches deleted: the polls bare-array fallback (the envelope is the only shape `buildFeedResponse` emits — an unrecognized payload now THROWS instead of degrading to an empty feed), the `placeName` alias (no server version emits it), and the `if (cacheRevealRequestId)` guard on a non-optional `string` whose only caller passes `x ?? createClientSearchRequestId()`.
F886 the slice-and-clear replaced by CHUNKING. It could not fire (flush at 50, `pending.size <= pendingEventCount()`) and would have silently discarded the remainder if it ever had; the server's 200 cap now holds regardless of what `FLUSH_AT_COUNT` becomes — silent loss is unrepresentable rather than merely unreachable.

'regular'` (closed union with a default), and FrostedGlass's `tintOpacity`/`tintColor` pair REPLACED by a `tintOverlay?: {color; opacity}` object with both fields required — the impossible states are gone, so there is nothing left to fall back from. The positioning model was previously inferred from `style`'s TRUTHINESS — any style at all silently turned the plate into a zero-size top-left box. **BEHAVIOR REPAIRS:**
F805/F831/F832 ONE exported request voice — `USER_INITIATED` / `SILENT`, typed as a real `AxiosRequestConfig` so they are directly passable (the smuggled-extra-keys problem was itself the defect). search.ts's `OPTIONAL_AUTH_REQUEST_CONFIG` and users.ts's inline object now BOTH resolve to `SILENT`. F831's live defect is closed: the three POLLED messaging reads (15s/15s/5s) pass `SILENT`, so a poll can no longer defeat the banner's own recovery loop (probe clears → next tick repaints, forever, over unrelated screens). NOT DONE, deliberately: inverting the interceptor's DEFAULT to silent. It is the shape that makes forgetting impossible, but it mutes the banner for every call site in one step, and "the banner no longer appears when it should" is a regression no type or unit test here can catch — it wants a sim pass over the failure matrix (`set_system_offline`). Recorded inline at the constants.
F833 `listMessages`'s `{cursor?, after?}` options DELETED. Both were dead (the one caller passes neither) and `after` advertised a capability mobile structurally cannot use — the server's contract is a TUPLE (`after` + `afterMessageId`) and mobile's signature had no `afterMessageId`, so a sender passing `after` alone would lose or duplicate same-millisecond messages. The surface no longer implies a capability.
F834 the share slug is THREADED. `sharedEntitySlug` added to the mobile fan-out payload (the server DTO has always accepted and persisted it) and `handleSend` now resolves it — minting via `enableShare` behind the existing owner-consent modal — BEFORE fanning out. ### honest coverage split (this territory, after this pass)

Territory totals before: 143 PARTIAL, 21 REDERIVED, 2 DELETED = 166 rows. After: **96 IDEAL-VERIFIED, 50 PARTIAL, 3 DELETED, 17 REDERIVED = 166.**

- **143 PARTIAL rows read line-by-line.** 1 was PHANTOM (F1358) and is now DELETED.
- **96 rows → IDEAL-VERIFIED**, each carrying its OWN one-line argument in COVERAGE (no row was given a generic one): overwhelmingly the pure contract/snapshot modules, the seven identical layout state-controllers, the reducers with spec pins, and the composition roots whose `dispose` tears down in exact reverse construction order.
- **46 of the read rows stay PARTIAL**, each now naming the specific F13xx that keeps it open — a far more useful state than the `F900-F984` cluster reference they all carried before.
- **17 rows keep their pass-1 REDERIVED status UNTOUCHED** because this pass did not read them (`AppRouteCoordinator.tsx`, the `transition-engine/` set incl. the F905/F920 SKIPPED-FOREIGN pair, the policy controllers/registry, `app-route-scene-runtime.ts`, `app-route-sheet-snap-session-runtime.ts`, and three specs). A first cut of this reconciliation swept them into IDEAL-VERIFIED as a side effect of a status rewrite; that would have been the exact dishonesty this pass exists to correct, and they were restored from HEAD.
- **4 rows DOWNGRADED from REDERIVED to PARTIAL** (`app-route-scene-stack-runtime.ts`, `app-route-scene-switch-controller.ts`, `app-route-sheet-host-authority-controller.ts`, `MainLaunchCoordinator.tsx`). These are the jumbos that had only ever been SPOT-read; the full read found F1350/F1351/F1354/F1355/F1356/F1357. Calling them REDERIVED was the pass-1 optimism this pass exists to correct.

### what was NOT found (the new baseline, re-checked not re-litigated)

The transition engine's one-notify-per-operation and supersede-terminates-armed-waits both hold at the one consumer in this territory that depends on them (`app-route-scene-stack-runtime.ts:2077-2116` — F904's fix is correct as written: it watches the txn it ARMED for, so a supersede terminates the wait instead of rearming). `SEEDED_FORWARD_OPEN` and the residency-identity Record are exhaustive. The scroll-state and pending-asset LRUs are bounded. `MOUNTED_BODY_BY_KEY` is total. F905/F920 were left alone as instructed. **Class 3 (unbounded lifetime) produced exactly ONE hit in the whole territory — F1350** — because nearly every map here is keyed by the closed `OverlayKey` vocabulary; the leak is in the one place keyed by a MONOTONE COUNTER instead. That is the generalizable lesson of this pass.

F1500 | search-flow-camera | apps/mobile/src/overlays/searchRouteSessionTypes.ts:33-56 + apps/mobile/src/navigation/runtime/app-overlay-route-types.ts:589 | THE HEADLINE: THE ORIGIN SNAPSHOT HAS NO CAMERA. `OriginSnapshot` = {sceneKey, sceneParams, detent, segment, scroll, anchor}. The owner's D55 law ("the map returns to the EXACT position where the search flow was triggered") is therefore served by a SEPARATE, older, cruder mechanism (F1501) that was never reconciled with the foundation. F1512 | search-flow-camera | plans/return-to-origin-foundation-design.md (whole) vs the shipped code | PLAN ARCHAEOLOGY VERDICT (D55 step 2). The design is ACCURATE and was largely EXECUTED, but its scope was the sheet and it drifted in three ways: (1) P0-P5 shipped in a different shape than written — the per-scene `registerOriginCaptureProvider` registry was collapsed into one rule (`buildCurrentOriginSnapshot`: home roots degenerate, everything else rich via a published live-state hook), which is BETTER than the plan (a scene opts in with one publication call, zero registration) and should be recorded as an improvement, not a deviation; (2) the plan's `childAnchor`→`anchor` P4 phase is VAPORWARE and the type now says so out loud (searchRouteSessionTypes.ts:50-55: "the origin-anchor SEAM (currently unwritten)… the old childAnchor slot-threading died with the re-push machinery") — so the "return to the exact comment span you searched from" half of the D55 law has NO mechanism today, in either the sheet or the camera lane; (3) the plan never contained a camera phase at all (F1500). The primitive that was considered and REJECTED and is worth re-raising: the plan chose "reconstruct-everywhere for V1 (not react-freeze)" and explicitly deferred freeze as "a later pure optimization for cheap origins" — a camera is the cheapest possible origin (two floats) and is the one field where freeze-and-replay is trivially correct. | RECORDED — archaeology, feeds F1513 | full read of the design + diff against the shipped controller | PHASE-3 (2026-08-05): RE-VERIFIED — searchRouteSessionTypes.ts:50-53 (line numbers shifted slightly, content unchanged) still reads "the origin-anchor SEAM (currently unwritten)… the old childAnchor slot-threading died with the re-push machinery", confirming the anchor gap this row identified is still real. This row is a plan-archaeology verdict, not itself a code defect (F1515 carries the live runtime consequence). | STATUS: OWNER-DECISION | TRIAGE (2026-08-05, bucket b/OWNER'S — REWRITTEN FOR A ONE-SITTING ANSWER): QUESTION: the D55 law promised 'return to the exact comment span you searched from' after a camera-origin round trip; the plan's own P4 childAnchor->anchor phase is vaporware (the type comment says so: 'the origin-anchor SEAM (currently unwritten)'), and this is true for BOTH the sheet and the newer camera lane. Build the anchor-publication mechanism (a departing scene publishes its own anchor via the origin live-state registry, per the existing comment's own description), or explicitly drop that half of the D55 law? OPTIONS: (1) Build the anchor seam — scoped design pass, not a quick fix. (2) Drop the 'exact comment span' promise — degrade to 'return to the scene/tab' (which does work today) and update the D55 law's stated scope to match. RECOMMENDATION: none offered — this is a real product-quality bar (how precisely does 'go back' need to feel) that trades an unscoped design effort against a known UX downgrade, exactly the kind of call this task should not make unilaterally. COST: (1) = a scoped design pass across the sheet + camera lanes; (2) = a documentation change, but a real (if narrow) UX regression from what D55 originally promised.

Source of the captured value: `ViewportBoundsService.getCamera()` (the atomic viewport-event camera, already the search lane's single source), NOT `lastCameraStateRef` (F1507). | RED-TEAM (the four real objections, answered in the return): in-flight programmatic camera at capture time; the deliberate "list world is bounds-independent" separation; home/degenerate byte-identity (the golden `assertDegenerateHomeEmission` contract); and whether a lens flip / user pan after the trigger should invalidate the origin. | IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-03 as approved (D56). D58-X1 (F1650 step 1) | maestro + mobile-nav-overlays | apps/mobile/src/navigation/runtime/app-route-persistent-header-registry.ts + PersistentSheetHeaderHost.tsx + 5 panel registrations | **FIXED — AND F1650's ATTRIBUTION IS CORRECTED BY THE FIX.** The six labels did not "need to go back on ToggleStrip": 9ad80e338 and its follow-ups replaced six per-panel close buttons with ONE host-owned `HeaderNavAction`, whose label was the generic `'Close page' / 'Create'` for every scene in the app — so the a11y defect was not "no label", it was "one label for every surface", which is worse than F1650 read it (a screen-reader user could not tell what the X dismisses, on ANY sheet). So "activate" does not mean "finish an unfinished feature"; it means BUILD A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION OF A SHIPPED ONE. **Activation cost, itemized:** the three named hooks on iOS, on top of un-freezing `active: false` — which is not a value but a TYPE (`readonly active: false` at :57, `active: false` at :32 of the runtime snapshot type), so activation is a type-level rewrite of the public surface, not a wiring change; then `syncNativeSnapshot` (target-runtime.ts:140, verified 2 hits: its type decl at :34 and itself) needs a real call site; then the six unwired registry methods of F1069(b) (re-verified this pass — each has exactly its type decl, its wrapper, and the wrapper's own native call, zero external callers); then the SAME three hooks again in 452 lines of Java if Android parity is meant (plans/android-parity.md); and finally a decision about what happens to the shipped hit-target path that the new one would replace. **Deletion scope, exact:** 1,244 JS lines + 529 Swift lines + 452 Java lines + one `RCT_EXTERN_MODULE(SearchChromeScalarSurfaceRegistry, NSObject)` block (UIFrameSamplerBridge.m:100-131, 32 lines) = **~2,257 lines**, and TWO live per-render call sites stop paying a bridge crossing for nothing (SearchShortcutsRow.tsx:41-42, SearchOverlayHeaderChrome.tsx:105 — each mount fires an async `registerMeasuredControl` promise into native). F1707 | mobile-native | apps/mobile/ios/cravesearch/UIFrameSampler.swift:2-6,155-158,226-232 | **THE UI-FRAME SAMPLER'S DROPPED-FRAME FIELDS ARE STRUCTURALLY INFLATED ON PROMOTION HARDWARE — A METRIC THAT CANNOT SHOW HONEST RED, IN THE ONE FILE WHOSE JOB IS TRUTHFUL MEASUREMENT.** `resolveDisplayHz()` returns `UIScreen.main.maximumFramesPerSecond` (120 on a ProMotion device), and `flushWindow` computes `expectedFrames = elapsedWindowMs / (1000/displayHz)` then `droppedFrameEstimate = max(0, expectedFrames - frameCount)` and `droppedFrameRatio`. But the `CADisplayLink` created at :98 is given NO `preferredFrameRateRange`, so on iOS 15+ ProMotion it defaults to the system's chosen cadence — routinely 60 while `maximumFramesPerSecond` reports 120. A perfectly smooth 60fps window therefore reports `droppedFrameRatio ≈ 0.5`. Both fields cross the bridge (`src/perf/ui-frame-sampler.ts:18-20` types `droppedFrameEstimate`, `droppedFrameRatio` and `displayHz`), so a consumer that ever gates on them gates on a lie. It does not currently affect the EMIT decision (`shouldEmit` at :159 uses avgFps/floorFps only, both computed from real inter-frame deltas and both honest) — which is why this is a latent instrument defect, not a live alarm, and why it is exactly the CLAUDE.md class: "a metric that can only ever show red is lying" is the mirror of "always green", and this one is stuck red-ish on the newest hardware and correct on the simulator, which is the worst possible place for it to be right. **Honest caveat: unproven at runtime** — the iPhone simulator reports 60, so it will not reproduce there; confirming it needs a real ProMotion device, which is why the fix should be the one that does not require the measurement (`link.preferredFrameRateRange = .init(minimum: 60, maximum: Float(displayHz), preferred: Float(displayHz))`, or derive `expectedFrames` from `link.targetTimestamp - link.timestamp` rather than from the screen's maximum). Cleanup-only, no behavior. | Ladder: `maximumFramesPerSecond` is the obvious reading of "how fast should this screen be" and was right in the 60Hz-only era. Bedrock = an instrument's denominator comes from the SAME clock as its numerator — ask the display link what it is actually targeting, never the screen what it is capable of. Rederive: pin the link's rate range (making the denominator true by construction) or compute expected frames from the link's own timestamps. | **ESCALATED** — the import cleanup is drive-by-safe; the rate-range fix wants the device measurement CLAUDE.md's methodology demands before a perf change is trusted, so it is proposed, not applied. | read the file in full; `grep -c "CLLocation\|MapboxMaps\.\|Turf\.\|LineString\|Point("` → 0; JS-side type surface in src/perf/ui-frame-sampler.ts:18-20 | STATUS: OPEN (was: ESCALATED/OWNER-DECISION) | NEXT ACTION: Two independent fixes, one file (UIFrameSampler.swift): (1) drop-in-cleanup — delete unused CoreLocation/MapboxMaps/Turf imports (verified 0 symbols used). (2) the ProMotion dropped-frame inflation fix needs a real device measurement before landing (CLAUDE.md's attribute-first law) — pin the CADisplayLink's preferredFrameRateRange or derive expectedFrames from the link's own timestamps rather than the screen's maximum. F1830 | api-user-surfaces (messaging) | apps/api/src/modules/messaging/messaging.service.ts:791-878 (`decorateConversations`, the `unreadCount` field computed inside `rows.map(async (row) => {...})` at line 848) | N+1 IN THE PRIMARY DM-INBOX READ PATH — the same disease F660 just cured for the header badge (`unreadCount()`, one `$queryRaw` aggregate for the whole page), left un-cured in `listConversations`/`getConversation`/`getOrCreateConversation`, all of which route through `decorateConversations`. For a page of N conversations (default 20, cap 50 via `ListConversationsQueryDto.limit`) the method already does 4 batched reads (blocks, follows, viewer-sent, last-messages) and then issues ONE ADDITIONAL `prisma.message.count()` PER ROW inside the map — up to 21 (limit+1 for hasMore) extra round-trips on the endpoint the client hits every time the DM inbox screen opens, which is materially more often than the polled badge F660 fixed. Concretely verified by reading lines 846-857: `unreadCount` is computed per-row with `take: UNREAD_DISPLAY_CAP` (confirmed at runtime this pass — Prisma's `count({take})` genuinely issues a `LIMIT`-bounded count, not a client-side no-op: tested live against a 174,240-row table, `count()` → 174240, `count({take:100})` → 100) but nothing batches the N per-row counts into the single aggregate query the sibling badge method already demonstrates is possible (a `GROUP BY conversation_id` raw query keyed on the SAME page's `conversationIds`, with `LEAST(count(*), 100)` per group). The comment at messaging.service.ts:788-790 documents "four batched reads... + one capped unread count per row" as if the per-row cost were accepted/intentional, but the immediately-adjacent F660 fix on the exact same file proves the team's own bar is "no N+1 for unread math" — this method just wasn't part of that pass. | Ladder: compensates-for = nothing (no batching exists for this call; `unreadCount()`'s aggregate is a SEPARATE method serving a different field — total badge count of conversations-with-unread, not per-conversation message counts — so it cannot be reused as-is, but the same raw-SQL technique directly generalizes: `GROUP BY conversation_id` with a `LEAST(count, 100)` cap, keyed on the page's `conversationIds` instead of the viewer's whole conversation set). bedrock = whether N extra round-trips per inbox-open is worth fixing now: the module's own comment calls conversation lists "launch scale... small," so this is real but bounded (worst case ~21 extra single-table indexed COUNT queries per page load, not unbounded fan-out) — flagged as OPEN rather than fixed inline per the audit's zero-blast-radius rule (this is a query-shape rewrite, not a typo). | STATUS: FIXED | NEXT ACTION: none — 2026-08-05: added `unreadCountsByConversation`, one `$queryRaw` `GROUP BY conversation_id` aggregate (`LEAST(count(*), UNREAD_DISPLAY_CAP)`, cap semantics identical to the reverted `count({take})`) joined per-row against EACH row's own participant cursor via `jsonb_to_recordset` (preserves the original per-row `lastReadMessageAt` cursor, not a single viewer-wide cutoff), batched into `decorateConversations`'s existing `Promise.all` as a 5th read. Read back via `Map<conversationId, number>`, defaulting absent rows to 0. `prisma.message.count` is no longer called anywhere in the file. F1831 | api-user-surfaces (notifications) | apps/api/src/modules/notifications/notification-dispatcher.service.ts:139-185 (`dispatchBatch`) + :60-94 (`dispatchPending`'s `sending`-reclaim arm) | A NOTIFICATION CAN BE DELIVERED TWICE ON A CRASH BETWEEN THE EXPO POST SUCCEEDING AND THE ROW BEING MARKED `sent`. `dispatchBatch` sets every row in the batch to `sending` (attempts+1) BEFORE the `fetch`, then awaits Expo's response and only afterward calls `applyReceipt`/`markFailed` per row. If the process dies (deploy, OOM, crash) after Expo has accepted and delivered the batch but before the `applyReceipt` writes land, the row is stuck in `sending`. `dispatchPending`'s reclaim arm (by design, F641, correctly fixing the PRIOR bug where this state was stranded forever) picks it back up once `updatedAt` is older than `RETRY_BACKOFF_MS` (5 min) and `attempts < MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS` — and resends the SAME push to the SAME device, because Expo's push API has no idempotency key / dedupe-by-request concept the code can hand it. This is the direct, unavoidable trade-off of making delivery durable (F640/F641's whole point was "never silently lose a push") — a false-negative-tolerant queue that leans toward at-least-once will, by construction, occasionally double-send rather than occasionally drop. Not a code defect relative to its own design; flagged because the task explicitly named "a notification that can be delivered twice... on retry" as this territory's risk to hunt, and no comment in the file currently states this trade-off as a conscious choice the way the `sending`-reclaim block's other comments do. | Ladder: compensates-for = nothing catches this (no idempotency key is sent to Expo, and none of Expo's documented push-ticket fields function as a dedupe key on the SEND side — Expo assigns ticket ids only in the RESPONSE, too late to prevent a resend of an already-in-flight request). bedrock = at-least-once delivery with no vendor-side idempotency is an accepted, common trade-off for push (a duplicate poll-release notification is a minor annoyance, not data loss or a billing event), so this is a documentation gap plus a possible severity-reduction lever, not a broken mechanism. | STATUS: OPEN | NEXT ACTION: either (a) accept as a known, low-severity trade-off and add one comment at the `sending` reclaim arm stating it explicitly (so a future reader doesn't mistake the current silence for "this was never considered"), or (b) if duplicate pushes prove to matter in practice, tighten `RETRY_BACKOFF_MS` risk by writing the Expo ticket id returned in a successful response onto the row synchronously with the SAME update that would mark it `sent` (already true) and additionally shortening the reclaim window is not a fix (races remain) — the only real fix is content-based client-side dedupe (the mobile push handler dedupes by `pollIds`+`placeId` already present in the payload), which is a mobile-side, not API-side, change; no API-side action recommended beyond (a).

F1850 | api-content-processing (reddit-collector) | apps/api/src/modules/content-processing/reddit-collector/reddit-batch-processing.service.ts:410-459 (`resolveLlmPosts` per-post fetch loop, shared by the chronological AND keyword batch workers) | A PER-POST FETCH FAILURE IS SILENTLY DROPPED WITH NO TOMBSTONE, NO METRIC, AND NO RETRY — indistinguishable in the returned result from "this post was legitimately skipped by the freshness/delta gate." For each `postId` in `fetchPostIds`, `redditService.getCompletePostWithComments` is awaited in a try/catch; a `RedditGovernanceDenialError` correctly rethrows (the worker requeues the whole batch), but every OTHER error (a transient 5xx, a timeout, a malformed/empty `rawResponse`, a post that 404s without the caller's typed `RedditApiError` path, `filterAndTransformToLLM` returning no `post`) is caught, logged at `error` level (`Failed to retrieve post ${postId}`), and the loop simply `continue`s — the post never enters `llmPosts`. The caller (`processBatch`) then reports `success: true` with `metrics.postsProcessed = llmPosts.length` — a count that is silently smaller than `job.postIds.length` with no field anywhere in `BatchProcessingResult` (`refetchGateSummary` only tracks `skippedDueToFreshness`/`skippedDueToDeltaThreshold`, both computed BEFORE this loop) that says "N posts were dropped because their fetch failed." Compare this to the SAME file's sibling machinery for the exact same problem one call away: `ChronologicalCollectionWorker.sweepOrphanCommentParents` (chronological-collection.worker.ts:754-798) hits an analogous fetch failure and explicitly (a) tombstones a genuine 404/no-post response via a `collectionRelevanceVerdict` row with `reason: 'parent_unfetchable'` so the post is never silently retried-forever nor silently re-dropped, and (b) leaves transient failures for the next tick with a `logger.warn`. The main batch fetch loop has neither of those — a deleted/unfetchable post referenced by a chronological or keyword listing (deleted between listing and fetch is a normal Reddit race) is dropped once, forever, with zero durable record, and a persistently-erroring subreddit (e.g. a sustained 5xx window) silently loses posts on every batch that touches them, since nothing throws to trigger Bull's 3-attempt retry and nothing re-queues the specific failed ids. | Ladder: compensates-for = nothing — `refetchGateSummary` is the only structured signal downstream reads, and it does not carry this count; the only trace is a `grep`-only error log line per post, which the task's own instructions call out as a diagnostic that "logs only on failure so silence cannot be told from a dead sampler." bedrock = the archive worker path is NOT affected (archive batches carry pre-transformed `llmPosts`, never hit this fetch loop) — this is specific to chronological + keyword, both of which route through `RedditBatchProcessingService.processBatch`. | STATUS: FIXED | NEXT ACTION: none — 2026-08-05: added a `skippedDueToFetchFailure` counter to `resolveLlmPosts`, threaded through `processBatch`'s log stage, the skipped-batch `warnings` message (now names fetch failures separately from freshness/delta gate skips), and both `refetchGateSummary` emission sites (`batch-processing-queue.types.ts` grew the matching field). Failures are split DECISIVE (empty `rawResponse`, failed `filterAndTransformToLLM`, or a caught `RedditApiError` with `statusCode === 404`) vs TRANSIENT (any other caught error), mirroring `sweepOrphanCommentParents` exactly: decisive failures get a new `tombstoneUnfetchablePosts` helper that writes `collectionRelevanceVerdict` rows (`keep: false, reason: 'fetch_failed_decisive', model: 'reddit-batch-fetch'`, best-effort — a tombstone write failure never fails the batch); transient failures are counted but not tombstoned, left for a future listing to re-surface the id. No change to what gets collected, the fetch plan, or cadence — reporting only, per the task's money/data-safety rule. If a user changes their locale mid-session (D4 ratified: request header + a user PROFILE override, not just device locale) within a cache entry's TTL, a repeated identical-payload search/profile fetch will silently serve the STALE-LOCALE cached response instead of re-hitting the network — exactly the shape plans/multilingual.md's own M1 checklist calls out and marks unfinished ("caches carrying rendered text key on it. (Today: locale is captured at device auth and read by NOTHING.)") plus the exact bug shape CLAUDE.md cites from the api autocomplete precedent (key folds one dimension, the consumer folds another). Currently near-zero OBSERVABLE impact because `entity_labels` is unpopulated (M2's label sweep is still future work per `entity-display.service.ts`'s own header comment), so `displayLabel` resolves to plain `entity.name` for virtually everything regardless of locale today — but the wiring for it to become live (Accept-Language on the wire, server-side negotiation + a real per-locale label table) is already shipped, and nothing in the client cache layer would catch the day it starts mattering. `/search/restaurants/:id/profile` (the restaurantProfileCache) doesn't even participate in locale negotiation server-side yet (no `@RequestLocale()` param on `restaurantProfile()`), so that cache is not at risk from this specific mechanism today. | Ladder: compensates for nothing today (M2 label sweep hasn't landed, so the two locales' responses are currently byte-identical in practice) — this is a landmine, not a live-observed defect; bedrock = plans/multilingual.md's own M1 ruling naming this exact gap, cross-checked against the shipped Accept-Language wiring in api.ts + search.controller.ts + entity-display.service.ts, which prove the "not yet" half of M1 is done while the "caches key on it" half is not. Rederive: fold `getCurrentLocale()` into `buildSearchCacheKey`'s cache-key input (or clear all three caches on a locale change) before M2 ships translated labels — cheap now, expensive to trace once real users see it as "search results randomly show English after I changed my language." | STATUS: FIXED (was: OPEN) | NEXT ACTION: none — closed. `buildSearchCacheKey` now folds `getCurrentLocale()` (imported from `../i18n/current-locale`, the exact cell api.ts's interceptor reads for `Accept-Language`) into the JSON stringified key for all three caches, folded once inside the shared builder so no call site (natural/structured/profile) can forget it — chosen over a locale-change cache-clear listener because folding-into-the-key makes a stale-locale hit structurally impossible (a new locale can never collide with an old entry) rather than dependent on a listener firing correctly. Does not conflict with plans/multilingual.md's M2 (entity_labels sweep) — it closes exactly the M1 gap that plan names as unfinished. Mutation-proven: apps/mobile/src/services/search-cache-locale.spec.ts (2 tests) goes RED under the reverted key (`api.post` called once instead of twice across a locale change) and GREEN with the fix; `diff` against `git show HEAD:...search.ts` confirmed the revert was real. Verify: tsc 0, yarn jest src 121/121 suites green.

REDERIVED RATHER THAN PATCHED: the missing distinction is not 'is this url well-formed' but 'may this environment invent one at all'. FIX:`getDatabaseUrl(env = process.env)`returns an explicitly-set DATABASE_URL verbatim in every environment; when it is ABSENT it throws if`isDeployedEnv(resolveAppEnv(env))`, and only then falls back on dev. NODE_ENV=test keeps its isolated-db fallback (a toolchain fact, not an AppEnv). WHY HERE AND NOT IN THE VALIDATOR: this is the SINGLE producer of `database.url`(one call site, configuration.ts:178 wait -- verified single use), so no caller can route around it; and by the time the validator sees a string, the information that would answer the question (was this chosen or invented?) has already been destroyed. That is what makes it an abstraction rather than a convention. SCOPE HELD DELIBERATELY TIGHT: absence only; nothing about what any environment CONNECTS to changed. RED-TEAM / WHAT IT MAKES IMPOSSIBLE: a deployed boot with a defaulted database url. What it does NOT make impossible: an explicitly-SET implausible url on a deployed env (see F2101). NOTE: the validator's`if (!url)`branch is now provably DEAD CODE in every environment (deployed throws upstream; dev/test always get a string) and should be deleted or re-pointed when that file is next clean — it was dirty in another session's tree during this pass and was NOT touched. MUTATION PROOF: replaced the`if (isDeployedEnv(appEnv))`predicate with`if (false as boolean)`; CONFIRMED THE REVERT LANDED BY GREP (`if (isDeployedEnv(appEnv))`count went 1 -> 0,`if (false as boolean)`count 0 -> 1) rather than assuming the regex matched; the two guard cases went RED and ONLY those two, while the dev-fallback and honour-verbatim cases stayed GREEN, proving the assertions are directional rather than vacuous (an over-eager fix that dropped the fallback everywhere fails the dev case). Restored, re-grepped (1 / 0), 10/10 GREEN. Three pre-existing F404 cases in the same spec simulated deployed envs with no DATABASE_URL and correctly began failing; each was given an explicit url, which is what a deployed env genuinely requires. eslint clean,`tsc --noEmit`clean,`yarn invariants`re-run. | STATUS: FIXED

The config it sat above read `testMatch: ['**/*.spec.ts?(x)']`, which DOES match `.tsx`. So anyone adding `'tsx'` to moduleFileExtensions (a natural, unrelated-looking change, e.g. to import a component from a spec) would silently begin pulling `.spec.tsx` component files into a `testEnvironment: 'node'` project with no `.tsx` transform, while the comment directly above insisted that could not happen. (packages/shared is a false alarm on inspection — its `build:types` runs `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly`, so it is compiled during build; only mobile is genuinely unchecked.) | ATTEMPTED THE OBVIOUS FIX AND BACKED IT OUT, WHICH IS THE FINDING'S REAL VALUE. Added `"type-check": "tsc --noEmit"` to apps/mobile/package.json; it is GREEN standalone (`yarn --cwd apps/mobile type-check` -> 0 errors, and `turbo run type-check --filter=@crave-search/mobile --force` -> 2/2 successful). BISECTED: mobile alone passes; `--filter=@crave-search/mobile --filter=api` fails; `--concurrency=1` passes. ROOT CAUSE: `packages/shared`'s `build` script begins `yarn clean` (`rm -rf dist`), and api's task chain rebuilds shared concurrently, so mobile's tsc reads `packages/shared/dist/index.d.ts` mid-deletion. Adding `"dependsOn": ["^build"]` to turbo.json's type-check task does NOT fix it (still 3/3 red) because the edge orders the build, not the concurrent DELETE. QUESTION: how should the workspace guarantee a producer's dist is intact while a consumer type-checks it? OPTIONS: (1) make `packages/shared`'s build non-destructive — drop `yarn clean` from `build` (tsup and tsc both overwrite; keep `clean` as its own script) so no task ever deletes an artefact a peer is reading, then add the mobile `type-check` script; ~30 min, and it fixes the latent flakiness of the api/site checks too. (2) Give mobile a `type-check` that does not cross the package boundary (path-map `@crave-search/shared` to `packages/shared/src` in apps/mobile/tsconfig.json), decoupling it entirely; also fixes it, but changes what mobile compiles against versus what it ships against. (3) Serialize the CI step (`turbo run type-check --concurrency=1`); one line, hides the underlying hazard, and slows the gate. RECOMMENDATION: (1) — it is the only option that removes the hazard rather than routing around it, and the destructive `clean` inside `build` is the actual defect. COST: ~30 min plus one CI run to confirm; unblocks F1791 as a side effect. | executed: turbo --dry=json command resolution, 3x --force runs, filter bisection, --concurrency=1 control | RESOLVED BY THIS PASS: turbo type-check now resolves real commands for all four packages (mobile and shared had NO type-check script; both resolved to <NONEXISTENT> and counted as success). `dependsOn: ["^build"]` added. F2307 | mobile-search (PHASE-1 MAP&HUNT) | apps/mobile/src/screens/Search/utils/price.ts:1-89 (whole file; NO spec exists) | TWO INCOMPATIBLE NUMBER SCALES SHARE ONE TYPE, SO SWAPPING THEM IS SILENT. The file maintains a "level" scale (1..4, a real Google price level) and a "slider" scale (1..5, where the max is an EXCLUSIVE right BOUNDARY), and converts between them (`buildLevelsFromRange`, `getRangeFromLevels`, `toPriceLevelRange`). But every one of those functions takes and returns `PriceRangeTuple = [number, number]` — the SAME structural type — so a level-range and a boundary-range are indistinguishable to tsc. `formatPriceRangeSummary` expects a BOUNDARY range and internally calls `toPriceLevelRange`; hand it an already-converted level range and it silently renders one band too narrow, with no error anywhere. The branded types that would prevent this already exist in the file (`PriceLevelValue`, `PriceSliderValue`) but the TUPLE type discards them. Compounding it: `clampPriceLevelValue` and `clampPriceSliderValue` are the same six lines with different bounds (duplicated logic, two places for a rounding bug to live), and the file has NO spec — the `min === max` widening rule at :40-46 and the empty-levels default at :62-63 are unexercised by any test. LADDER: compensates-for = a slider UI that needs N+1 stops to express N selectable bands, colliding with a server contract in levels. Bedrock = the two scales are genuinely different domains; the type system is the only thing that can keep them apart at a call site, and `[number, number]` refuses the job. (a) SILENTLY EXEMPT — 112 rows carrying a REVIEWED status (IDEAL-VERIFIED/REDERIVED/PARTIAL/FIXED) have a non-hex first token: `Read`, `npx`, `Prompt`, `NEW`, `(uncommitted)`, `PHASE-3-W3`, `F1970:`, plus 18 bare `-`. coverage-staleness.mjs:83 `if (!/^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/.test(...)) continue;` skips them AFTER `reviewed += 1`, with no counter and no message. Those rows can never go stale no matter how far their file drifts, and `--check` (CI, ci.yml:103) exits 0. This is precisely the repo's own named anti-pattern: a guard whose failure case is unreachable, reporting completeness it did not measure. (b) PERMANENTLY STALE — 113 UNREVIEWED rows carry a COMMIT sha in the blob column and 36 carry an object that does not exist at all; a commit sha can never equal a blob sha, so those rows are reverted to UNREVIEWED on EVERY run, forever, regardless of how carefully they were reviewed. 46 of the 110 UNREVIEWED rows in this pass's four territories (42%) are in this class. That converts 112 silent exemptions and 149 permanent-stale rows into one loud, fixable list, and makes the "0 STALE" line mean what it says. Then repair the 149 mis-recorded rows by resolving `git show <commit>:<path>` where a commit sha was recorded. | STATUS: OPEN | NEXT ACTION: Orchestrator approves the coverage-staleness.mjs change (blob-type assertion + hard fail on non-blob/absent sha) and the one-time repair of the 149 rows; until then treat every "IDEAL-VERIFIED" row with a non-hex sha as UNVERIFIED, and expect the 36 byte-identical rows re-verified in this pass to be erased again by the next `--apply` unless their shas are written as blob shas.

F2700 | api-external-integrations (money/spend — durability of the meter) | apps/api/src/modules/external-integrations/shared/usage-ledger.service.ts:143-149 vs 266-269, 293-296, 351-354; apps/api/src/modules/external-integrations/governance/pool-registry.ts:754-767, 817-836; governance.service.ts (no `onModuleDestroy` — grep over the file returns zero hits) | THE LEDGER ROW IS AWAITED ON SHUTDOWN; THE DOLLAR DEBIT THAT FEEDS THE CATASTROPHE BACKSTOP IS NOT. `UsageLedgerService` maintains a `pending` Set explicitly so "short-lived scripts and deploys can't drop records" (line 143-145) and `onModuleDestroy` awaits it — but ONLY the `apiUsageEvent.createMany` promise is ever added to that Set (line 216). All three spend meters are launched as bare `void this.governance.pools.meterSpend(...)` and are tracked by nothing: not by `pending`, not by a `GovernanceService.onModuleDestroy` (there is none), not by `PoolRegistry` (it has no shutdown hook either). `meterSpend` -> `consumeMetered` -> `flushDurable`, and `flushDurable` runs behind `serializeDurable`'s per-pool promise CHAIN (pool-registry.ts:341-349), so it is not merely one racing round-trip — it can be queued arbitrarily far behind other in-flight flushes for the same pool. The in-memory `consume()` is synchronous, so the process's own view is right; what is lost is the durable `pool_window_consumption` write. Consequence, and it is asymmetric in the dangerous direction: after a script exit or a container stop, the LEDGER (the accounting record) is complete while the POOL (the admission counter) under-counts by the dropped delta — and it is the pool, not the ledger, that `assertPlacesSpendOpen`/`assertGeminiSpendOpen`/`assertTomtomSpendOpen` read. Every drop makes the month's ceiling looser than it reads, silently and permanently (a monthly window is never recomputed from the ledger). This is the same defect class as the one usage-ledger.service.ts:235-245 already documents — "a gate reading a counter that is permanently zero admits forever" — one notch weaker: a counter that is merely LOSSY admits longer than it should. LADDER — what it compensates for: `pending` compensates for fire-and-forget being unsafe at shutdown; it was applied to the write whose loss is visible (a missing ledger row shows up in a cost report) and not to the write whose loss is invisible (a pool silently a few dollars low). BEDROCK: "a fire-and-forget write that governs admission must be drained before the process that issued it exits" — bedrock because there is no other actor that can replay it; the delta exists only in this process's `unpersisted` field. REDERIVE: the drain set belongs to whoever OWNS the in-flight promise. Today two owners each hold half. Either (a) `PoolRegistry` implements its own `onModuleDestroy` that awaits every `durableWriteChains` entry (it already has the exact Map needed, line 339), which makes it impossible for ANY caller of meterSpend/meter/reconcile/alignToVendor to leak — including the two in spend-campaign.service.ts and the boot re-registration at governance.service.ts:553 — or (b) usage-ledger adds these three promises to `pending`, which fixes three call sites and leaves the other three able to forget. RED-TEAM: (b) is convention (a fourth meter site can forget); (a) is abstraction — the registry cannot be constructed in a way that leaks, because the chain Map is where every durable write already lands. What (a) DELETES: nothing structural, but it retires the question "is this meter awaited?" at every present and future call site. THE MUTATION THAT PROVES IT: with a store whose `add` resolves after 50ms, call `meterSpend` then immediately `await app.close()`, and assert the store recorded the delta — RED today. NO SPEC EXERCISES SHUTDOWN AGAINST A POOL: `pool-registry.spec.ts` (731 lines) contains no `onModuleDestroy`/`close` case, so the suite is green in the lossy state. NOT MEASURED BY THIS PASS: how much money this has actually lost — that needs the prod `pool_window_consumption` sum vs the `api_usage_ledger` sum for the same month, which is a live-DB read I did not perform. | STATUS: OPEN | NEXT ACTION: orchestrator to approve option (a) — a `PoolRegistry.onModuleDestroy` (or explicit drain method called from GovernanceService's) that awaits every entry in `durableWriteChains`, plus the RED-provable spec above; and separately run the prod ledger-vs-pool reconciliation query to size the historical loss before deciding whether a one-off correction to the month's consumption row is warranted.
F2701 | api-external-integrations (money/spend — backstop derivation, ESCALATED) | apps/api/src/modules/external-integrations/shared/spend-analytics.service.ts:62-72, 862-1080 vs apps/api/src/modules/external-integrations/governance/governance.service.ts:366-437, 585-620 | THE ONLY VENDOR WHOSE CATASTROPHE CAP IS RE-DERIVED FROM MEASUREMENT — AND THE ONLY ONE THAT ALERTS WHEN THE DERIVATION DIES — IS THE ONE THE FILE ITSELF ARGUES IS THE CONVERGING, SMALLER RISK. `applyDerivedGeminiBackstop` reads the nightly `backstop.gemini/month` row, `resetLimit`s the pool to `BACKSTOP_MULTIPLE x` trailing MEASURED spend, re-checks health daily by riding the gate (governance.service.ts:728-737), and — the good part — emits a critical-path ops alert when NO derived row exists, with the reasoning stated out loud: "SILENCE HERE IS THE FAILURE MODE... an owner guess wearing a derivation's clothes, which SS16 exists to forbid." `googlePlaces.monthlySpend` ($200, `GOOGLE_PLACES_MONTHLY_SPEND_CAP_USD`) and `tomtom.monthlySpend` ($250, `TOMTOM_MONTHLY_SPEND_CAP_USD`) have NEITHER: no derivation job, no re-derivation, no staleness alert, no equivalent of the "you are running on the env seed" warning. WHAT MAKES THIS NOT MERELY COSMETIC IS THE REPO'S OWN ARGUMENT, at governance.service.ts:385-388: "Unlike TomTom, this spend does NOT converge: TomTom cost is per PLACE and a place is outlined once, so it asymptotes as your geography fills in, while Places is driven by user TEXT, which is infinite." And usage-ledger.service.ts:239-241 records that Places was 55% of a $565.80 month. So the vendor with unbounded growth and the largest historical line carries a hand-set number that nothing ever revisits, while the vendor with a bounded, measured, converging cost carries the automated derivation. NOT A DEFECT IN THE NO-FAKE-ESTIMATES SENSE — both numbers are legitimately typed as OWNER CHOICES and are documented as such ($200 "owner-priced 2026-08-01"; $250 shown as `3 x` a measured month at a vendor-verified rate). The gap is that an owner choice has no expiry and no alarm: if Places spend triples as the corpus grows, the $200 cap starts denying real enrichment with only the exhausted-backstop alert to say so, and if the owner raises it reactively there is no measurement anchoring the new value either. LADDER — bedrock: "a ceiling is either a measurement, or an owner choice that the system re-presents to the owner on a cadence." Gemini implements the first arm; Places/TomTom implement neither arm's feedback. Rederive: the SpendGateCopy record (governance.service.ts:117-148) already proves the three gates are ONE abstraction differing only in copy — the derivation is the one axis where they were not unified, and unifying it (a per-vendor `backstop.<vendor>` work_class, same nightly job, same underived alert) would make "a vendor with no derivation policy" unrepresentable. RED-TEAM: if instead we only add a staleness alert to the two env-seeded caps, a fourth vendor added tomorrow can still forget both — that is convention. ESCALATE, because the choice between (i) derive all three the way gemini is derived, (ii) keep Places/TomTom as owner dials but add a mandatory "this cap is N days old and month-to-date is X% of it" alert, or (iii) leave as-is, is a money-posture and product call, not a taste call I may make. COST: (i) ~a day (the derivation already exists; it needs a vendor dimension on the work_class and the same clamp/winsorize reasoning re-argued per vendor, because Places' distribution is not Gemini's); (ii) ~2 hours; (iii) zero. RECOMMENDATION: (ii) now, (i) when Places spend has enough trailing months to derive from — deriving a cap from a corpus that is still filling in would produce a ceiling that ratchets down on itself, which is precisely the failure `refreshBackstop`'s own clamp (spend-analytics.service.ts:978-980) exists to prevent for Gemini. | STATUS: ESCALATED | NEXT ACTION: owner decides between (i)/(ii)/(iii) above; I recommend (ii) — a staleness+headroom ops alert for `googlePlaces.monthlySpend` and `tomtom.monthlySpend`, deferring full derivation until there is a trailing window worth deriving from.

Lines 77-79 read: "The persisted subset — the three FILTER fields, and only those. Derived from one list so `partialize` and the migration's key-strip can never drift apart." `PERSISTED_KEYS` is then used by `migrate` (:126) and NOT by `partialize`, which hand-enumerates all four keys as an object literal (:183-188). So the two are exactly as free to drift as before the constant existed, and the comment is the only thing standing between a reader and that belief. (Note the comment ALSO says "three FILTER fields" while the list and the literal both carry FOUR — openNow, dietary, priceLevels, risingActive — a second, independent staleness in the same three lines.) The concrete failure: add a fifth persisted filter to `PERSISTED_KEYS` and `migrate` will carry it across a version bump while `partialize` never writes it, so it survives migration and then vanishes on the next save — a preference that appears to persist and silently does not. BEDROCK: "which fields outlive the process" is one fact; a list is the right home for it. That IS bedrock — it is not derivable from the state type (the tab fields are deliberately excluded, :20-23). REDERIVED: `partialize: (state) => Object.fromEntries(PERSISTED_KEYS.map((k) => [k, state[k]])) as Pick<SearchRuntimeMirroredState, PersistedKey>` — one list, both readers. RED-TEAM: what does it make impossible? Adding a key to the list and forgetting to persist it. What can a caller still forget? Adding the key to the list at all — but that failure is loud (the field is simply not persisted, with no comment claiming otherwise). WHAT IT DELETES: the four-line object literal and the false sentence above it. THE MUTATION THAT PROVES IT: append a throwaway key to `PERSISTED_KEYS` and assert `partialize` emits it; under today's code it does not. WHAT IS FINE AND WHY: the rest of this file is genuinely ideal — the R1c single-writer contract (:45-50) is stated AND structurally true (one exported verb, no per-field setters), `normalizePriceLevels` correctly collapses a full 1-4 selection to "no filter" rather than storing a tautology, the AsyncStorage wrapper degrades to an in-memory Map with a logged warning rather than throwing, and :20-23 explicitly REFUSES to silently answer the owner question about whether the tab preference should survive a cold start — that refusal is the right call and should be kept. | STATUS: OPEN | NEXT ACTION: derive `partialize` from `PERSISTED_KEYS` and correct the "three FILTER fields" count in the comment to four; no behavior change today (the two lists currently agree), so this is a pure unrepresentability fix.
F2802 | mobile-app-core (PHASE-1 MAP&HUNT) | apps/mobile/src/providers/AuthProvider.tsx:349-356, :360-371, :123, :326 | THE FILE STATES THE LAW "A `console.warn` IN THE AUTH/MONEY PATH IS INVISIBLE IN PRODUCTION" AND THEN APPLIES IT TO TWO OF ITS FOUR CATCHES — INCLUDING SKIPPING THE TWO RELEASE-ONLY GUARDS WHOSE COMMENTS CLAIM THEY ARE LOUD. F813's own words at :85-88: "routed through the crash-reporting seam. A `console.warn` in the AUTH/MONEY path is invisible in production — this is the seam App.tsx wires and whose own docstring states the law". `tokenCache.getToken` (:89) and `tokenCache.saveToken` (:104) obey it. Two others do not, and both are strictly higher-stakes: (a) `:123` — the Clerk token resolver's catch, `console.warn('[AuthProvider] Failed to fetch Clerk token')`, returning null, which api.ts's `getAuthToken` then swallows into an UNAUTHENTICATED request; (b) `:326` — the push registrar's whole-body catch, `console.warn('[Notifications] Failed to register push token')`, whose consequence is a user who receives zero push notifications forever with nothing anywhere saying why. WORSE, THE TWO RELEASE-BUILD GUARDS ARE STRUCTURALLY SILENT IN THE ONLY BUILD THEY TARGET. `:349-356` (release build with NO Clerk key → "the app would run fully UNAUTHENTICATED") and `:360-371` (release build carrying a `pk_test_` key → "users will authenticate against the test instance") are `console.error` calls gated on `!__DEV__`. VERIFIED against the seam they bypass: `src/observability/crash-reporting.ts:63-72` records that the house logger's console emission is already `__DEV__`-only precisely because "Console emission is now `__DEV__`-only and the production record lives here instead" — i.e. this repo has already ruled that a console line does not reach production. Sentry's default console-breadcrumb integration turns these into BREADCRUMBS, and a breadcrumb ships only attached to a later event; the failure mode here is an app that works fine and reports nothing, so no event follows and the breadcrumb dies in the 60-entry ring. Net: the guard for "we shipped a release with no auth" fires only into a channel that does not exist in a release build. `captureHandledError` is imported at :33 of this same file and used 30 lines above. BEDROCK: a misconfiguration that is invisible in the environment it can only occur in is not guarded. REDERIVED: both release guards call `captureHandledError(new Error(...), { seam: 'auth:missing-clerk-key' | 'auth:test-clerk-key' })` in addition to the console line; (a) and (b) likewise. RED-TEAM — what does this make impossible? Nothing yet: a future catch can still reach for `console.warn`. The real abstraction is an eslint rule banning bare `console.warn`/`console.error` outside `__DEV__` blocks in `src/providers`/`src/services`, which is exactly the door-lock-ban shape this repo already runs `scripts/check-lint-ban-inheritance.mjs` to protect. WHAT IS FINE AND WHY: `reportPushEnvironmentClassification` (:48-78) is a model instrument — it MEASURES the APNs environment at runtime rather than trusting the entitlements file, raises a handled error only for the genuinely broken combination (distributed build + non-production aps-environment), and can show RED; and `resolveHomeLocationSignal` (:181-215) correctly distinguishes revoked (explicit null) from unknown (omit the field) so the server cannot mistake "no fix right now" for "clear my home", with the three states named in both the client type and the DTO comment. | STATUS: OPEN | NEXT ACTION: route :123, :326 and BOTH release-build guards (:351, :366) through `captureHandledError` with distinct `seam:` tags, keeping the console lines for dev; then consider the eslint ban so the next catch cannot reintroduce it.

It is currently RED: `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/mobile/tsconfig.spec.json` = 8 errors (7 of them F2803's, 1 a `TS5097` on `src/tracksheet/__render__/mocks/runtime-mock.ts:52` importing a path ending in `.ts`). F2805 | mobile-app-core (PHASE-1 MAP&HUNT) | apps/mobile/src/services/api.ts:509-538 | THE BANNER RECOVERY PROBE CANNOT START AGAINST AN ISSUE THAT IS ALREADY LIVE WHEN IT MOUNTS — THE OWNERSHIP MOVE (F806) INTRODUCED A START-TIME STATE READ THAT NEVER HAPPENS. `startBannerRecoveryProbe` establishes the interval ONLY from inside `useSystemStatusStore.subscribe(...)`; zustand (v5.0.8, verified from `node_modules/zustand/package.json`) does not invoke a `subscribe` listener at subscription time, so if `serviceIssue != null` at the moment of the call, no timer is created and no probe runs until some LATER `setState`. The probe's own comment (:490-492) states the guarantee it then fails to hold: "A reported service issue must clear when HEALTH RETURNS — not only when some later user action happens to succeed (the old behavior left 'Service temporarily unavailable.' stuck indefinitely on an idle screen)" — which is verbatim the state this gap reproduces. Reachability, stated honestly rather than asserted: the probe is mounted by `NetworkStatusListener` (App.tsx:147), which sits above the auth tree and is not remounted on ordinary navigation, so the common cold-start ordering (mount, then a request fails) is safe. The gap is real for any remount-while-degraded — a Fast-Refresh of the listener in dev, a future move of the mount below a conditional, or any second caller — and for a store rehydrated with an issue already set. It is a latent always-green: nothing can distinguish "probe running" from "probe never started", because the only observable is the banner clearing, which a later successful request also does. BEDROCK: a subscription that drives an effect from state must reconcile against the CURRENT state at subscribe time; "react to changes" and "hold an invariant over state" are different jobs and only the latter is what this needs. REDERIVED: hoist the body to a named `sync(state)` and call `sync(useSystemStatusStore.getState())` once before subscribing (`subscribe` then passes each new state to the same function) — idempotent, since the body already guards on `healthProbeTimer == null`. RED-TEAM: makes impossible — a mount-order change silently disabling recovery. Still forgettable? No: there is one function and it is called from both edges. WHAT IT DELETES: the implicit "this is only ever mounted before any request" assumption, which is nowhere written down. THE MUTATION THAT PROVES IT: in a spec, `reportServiceIssue` FIRST, then `startBannerRecoveryProbe()`, and assert a health GET is attempted within one interval — RED today, green after. | STATUS: OPEN | NEXT ACTION: add the initial `sync(getState())` before `subscribe` in `startBannerRecoveryProbe`, plus the report-then-start spec above as the RED proof.

Consequence: the "a deleted account is its own story" block (:116-145) asserts only on the PURE function's return value — including two `expect(...).not.toBe(...)` negatives, which are the weakest assertion shape available — while the actual observable behavior the branch exists to produce (`useAccountDeletedStore.getState().announceDeleted(purgeDueAt)` flipping `deleted` and carrying the deadline the restore copy renders) is asserted nowhere in the repo. The strong form is to EXPORT the interceptor's dispatch from api.ts (or from api-failure-policy.ts as `applyApiFailureAction(action)`) and have both the interceptor and the spec call it, at which point drift is unrepresentable rather than merely noticed. THE MUTATION THAT PROVES IT: delete the `account_deleted` arm from api-failure-policy.ts — the whole suite still passes the store-transition assertions, because there are none. F3000 | api-external-integrations (LLM outage guard — held requests never book the window they fire in) | apps/api/src/modules/external-integrations/llm/rate-limiting/centralized-rate-limiter.service.ts:685-700 (throttled arm of reserveLocallyDuringOutage) + apps/api/src/modules/external-integrations/llm/rate-limiting/smart-llm-processor.service.ts:157-190 (caller sleeps then fires, no re-reserve on the outage path) | A THROTTLED OUTAGE RESERVATION IS A SLEEP, NOT A SLOT. When Redis is down and the local minute guard is full, the guard returns `{ throttled: true, reservationTime: nextMinuteBoundary }` WITHOUT incrementing any counter, and SmartLLMProcessor treats it like any reservation: sleep waitMs, then fire. So every request held out of minute N fires at the top of minute N+1 while minute N+1 separately admits its own full `limit` — up to 2x the per-replica ceiling lands in one minute, synchronized at the boundary (the guard's own "spread the allowance" pacing applies only to ADMITTED requests). The outage-guard spec (outage-guard.spec.ts:52-68) asserts the 61st is "held to the next window" but never asserts the next window's admission count includes it — the exact property the guard exists for. Not the original disease (unbounded concurrency after a 1.5s nap) but a factor-of-2 breach of the stated ceiling in exactly the burst shape 429s punish. PROVING MUTATION/SPEC: in outage-guard.spec, drive `limit+k` calls in minute N (k throttled), then at `now = N+1 boundary` drive `limit` more and assert total non-throttled releases landing in minute N+1 <= limit — fails today (limit+k fire). PROPOSAL: the throttled arm should book the held request into the NEXT minute's bucket (increment that bucket when returning the hold), or the caller should re-call the guard after sleeping on a throttled outage reservation. | STATUS: OPEN | NEXT ACTION: P2 books held requests into the destination minute's counter inside reserveLocallyDuringOutage (one-file change, spec above proves it RED first).
F3001 | api-places-enrichment (TomTom bbox parse re-breaks the antimeridian fix it sits next to) | apps/api/src/modules/places/tomtom-chain-probe.adapter.ts:1010-1029 (parseForwardBoundingBox) and :992-1007 (parseReverseBoundingBox) vs packages/shared/src/geo/place-geo.ts:206-211 (bboxContainsPoint, arc-aware, honors minLng>maxLng crossing representation) | Math.min/Math.max ON LONGITUDE DESTROYS THE CROSSING REPRESENTATION THE CONTAINMENT CHECK WAS TAUGHT TO READ. GeoBbox deliberately represents an antimeridian-crossing box as minLng>maxLng, and the 2026-07-26 fix (adapter comment at :727-731) moved candidate validation to bboxContainsPoint "by lng ARCS" precisely so wrap boxes stop being rejected. But both parsers still normalize with Math.min/max on lon: a vendor bbox topLeft.lon=170 / btmRight.lon=-170 (a 20-degree wrap box) parses to {minLng:-170, maxLng:170} — the 340-degree COMPLEMENT arc. Consequence: an anchor near 180 tests OUTSIDE the parsed bbox, so the anchor-containment fix silently rejects every genuinely-crossing candidate (node stays bbox-less forever — the pre-fix symptom, reintroduced one function lower), and if such a bbox IS ever stored (the free reverse bbox path stores without containment checking) the catalog holds a nearly-world-wide extent for a small place, and bboxes-only-grow means it can never shed it. Live exposure exists in the US: the Aleutian Islands (Alaska) cross the antimeridian. The forward shape already tells us which edge is which (topLeftPoint=NW, btmRightPoint=SE), so min/max is not needed for lng at all. PROVING MUTATION/SPEC: unit-test parseForwardBoundingBox with tl.lon=170, br.lon=-170 and assert the result contains point lng=179 via bboxContainsPoint — fails today. PROPOSAL (P2): lat keeps min/max; lng takes tl.lon->minLng, br.lon->maxLng verbatim (and reverse shape sw.lng->minLng, ne.lng->maxLng), preserving the crossing representation bboxContainsPoint/bboxContains already handle. | STATUS: OPEN | NEXT ACTION: P2 applies the two-line parser change with the RED spec above; audit places rows for stored bboxes where min_lng approx -180 and max_lng approx 180 on sub-country levels before/after.

RED-TEAM: the current shape makes nothing impossible — any new dep with unstable identity multiplies silent API calls. THE MUTATION THAT PROVES IT: log the effect body and drive the sim with a moving simulated location — one boot, N search POSTs (measure per attribution law before fixing; the fix is a hasPrefetchedRef latch or `startupLocationSnapshot?.coordinate?.lat/lng` scalar deps).
